Saṃyuktāgama: "Cutting the three fetters one becomes a stream-enterer, not subject to the lower realms, certain of awakening, being reborn at most seven times among gods and humans, reaching the end of suffering." The three fetters are self-view, clinging to rules and rituals, and doubt — abandoned at the path of seeing.

It is the decisive turn from ordinary being to noble one: having seen the truth, one no longer falls back.

quotes.text: 三結斷得須陀洹，不墮惡趣法，決定正趣三菩提，七有天人往生，究竟苦邊
quotes.note_en: Having cut the three fetters one attains stream-entry, is not subject to the lower destinies, is certain of right awakening, is reborn at most seven times among gods and humans, and reaches the end of suffering.

terms.root: sakṛt「一次」＋ āgāmin「來者」 · sakṛt "once" + āgāmin "one who comes"
terms.short_zh: 斷三結，貪瞋癡薄，只再往返人間一次即得解脫；四果之二果。
terms.short_en: Once-returner — three fetters cut and greed, hatred and delusion weakened; returns to this world only once more. The second fruit.
terms.detail_zh: 《雜阿含經》：「三結盡，貪、恚、癡薄，得斯陀含。」斯陀含在須陀洹的基礎上進一步削弱欲界的貪瞋，但尚未斷盡。
terms.detail_en: Saṃyuktāgama: "The three fetters ended, greed, hatred and delusion weakened, one attains once-returning." Building on stream-entry, the once-returner further weakens desire-realm greed and hatred, without yet ending them.

quotes.text: 貪、恚、癡薄，得斯陀含
quotes.note_en: Greed, hatred and delusion weakened, one attains once-returning.

terms.root: an-「不」＋ āgāmin「來者」 · an- + āgāmin "one who comes"
terms.short_zh: 斷五下分結，不再生於欲界，於色界、無色界證涅槃；四果之三果。
terms.short_en: Non-returner — five lower fetters cut, never reborn in the desire realm, attaining nirvāṇa in a higher realm. The third fruit.
terms.detail_zh: 《雜阿含經》：「五下分結盡，生般涅槃阿那含。」五下分結：身見、戒禁取、疑、欲貪、瞋恚——繫縛有情於欲界的五種煩惱。斷盡後不再還來欲界。
terms.detail_en: Saṃyuktāgama: "The five lower fetters ended, one is a non-returner attaining nirvāṇa upon rebirth [in a higher realm]." The five lower fetters — self-view, clinging to rules, doubt, sensual desire, ill will — bind beings to the desire realm; with them cut, one does not return here.

quotes.text: 五下分結盡，生般涅槃阿那含
quotes.note_en: The five lower fetters ended, one is a non-returner who attains parinirvāṇa after rebirth.

terms.short_zh: 斷盡一切煩惱、不再受生的聖者；聲聞乘的最高果位。
terms.short_en: Arhat — the noble one who has ended all afflictions and will not be reborn; the highest fruit of the disciple vehicle.
terms.detail_zh:
arhat 意為「值得（供養）者」，漢譯「應供」；又有「殺賊」（殺煩惱賊）、「不生」、「無學」（已無可學）之義。經中證阿羅漢者自說：「我生已盡，梵行已立，所作已作，自知不受後有。」

唯識說到阿羅漢位，末那不再執阿賴耶為我，故「阿羅漢位捨」阿賴耶之名。大乘認為阿羅漢已斷煩惱障，但未斷所知障。
terms.detail_en:
Arhat means "worthy (of offerings)", Chinese 應供; also glossed "slayer of the foe" (afflictions), "not reborn", "beyond training". Those attaining it declare: "Birth is ended, the holy life lived, what had to be done is done; I know there is no further existence."

Yogācāra says that at arhatship manas no longer grasps the store consciousness as self, so its name ālaya is "relinquished at arhatship". The Mahāyāna holds that arhats have ended the afflictive but not the cognitive obstruction.

quotes.text: 我生已盡，梵行已立，所作已作，自知不受後有。
quotes.note_en: My births are ended, the holy life is lived, what had to be done is done; I know for myself that there is no further existence.

terms.root: √budh「覺醒」的過去分詞 · past participle of √budh, "awakened"
terms.short_zh: 「覺者」：自覺、覺他、覺行圓滿者。有十種尊號。
terms.short_en: "The awakened one": awakened oneself, awakening others, perfect in awakening. Has ten epithets.
terms.detail_zh:
buddha 是 √budh（醒）的過去分詞，「醒過來的人」。自覺、覺他、覺行圓滿，是佛與二乘（只自覺）、菩薩（覺行未圓滿）的區別。

**十號**：《雜阿含經》：「如來、應、等正覺、明行足、善逝、世間解、無上士、調御丈夫、天人師、佛世尊。」
terms.detail_en:
Buddha is the past participle of √budh "to wake" — "one who has woken up". Awakened oneself, awakening others, perfect in awakening — distinguishing a buddha from the two vehicles (self-awakened only) and bodhisattvas (not yet perfect).

**Ten epithets** (Saṃyuktāgama): "Tathāgata, worthy, perfectly awakened, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, well-gone, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of those to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, Buddha, World-Honoured."

quotes.text: 如來、應、等正覺、明行足、善逝、世間解、無上士、調御丈夫、天人師、佛世尊
quotes.note_en: Tathāgata, worthy one, perfectly awakened, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, well-gone, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of those to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, Buddha, World-Honoured One.

terms.root: tathā「如此」＋ gata「去」／āgata「來」 · tathā "thus" + gata "gone" / āgata "come"
terms.short_zh: 佛的十號之首：「乘如實道而來」，或「如是去」。
terms.short_en: First of the Buddha's ten epithets — "thus come" by the path of suchness, or "thus gone".
terms.detail_zh: tathāgata 可拆為 tathā-gata（如是去）或 tathā-āgata（如是來）。漢譯「如來」取後者：乘真如之道而來成正覺。《金剛經》則破其相：「如來者，無所從來，亦無所去，故名如來。」
terms.detail_en: Tathāgata can be read tathā-gata "thus gone" or tathā-āgata "thus come". Chinese 如來 takes the latter: come by the path of suchness to perfect awakening. The Diamond Sūtra undercuts the image: "The Tathāgata comes from nowhere and goes nowhere; therefore he is called Tathāgata."

quotes.text: 如來者，無所從來，亦無所去，故名如來。
quotes.note_en: The Tathāgata does not come from anywhere, nor go anywhere; therefore he is called the Tathāgata.

terms.short_zh: 「任持自性，軌生物解」：一指佛陀的教法（三寶之法），二指一切現象（諸法）。
terms.short_en: "What holds its own nature": both the Buddha's teaching (the Dharma of the Three Jewels) and any phenomenon (dharmas).
terms.detail_zh:
dharma 源自 √dhṛ（持）。中國注家解為「任持自性，軌生物解」：能保持自己的特性，並成為令人理解的軌範。常見兩大意義：

1. **佛法、教法**：三寶中的「法」，佛陀所說的真理與教導；
2. **諸法、現象**：一切存在的構成要素，如百法、五蘊中的每一法。

另外「法處」「法界」的「法」專指意識所緣。《中阿含經》：「若見緣起便見法，若見法便見緣起。」
terms.detail_en:
Dharma comes from √dhṛ "to hold". Chinese commentators gloss it "holding its own nature, serving as a pattern that produces understanding". Two main senses:

1. **The Dharma, the teaching**: the Dharma of the Three Jewels, the truth taught by the Buddha;
2. **dharmas, phenomena**: the constituents of existence, e.g. each of the hundred dharmas or the elements of the aggregates.

And in "dharma base/element" it means specifically the object of mind. Madhyamāgama: "Whoever sees dependent origination sees the Dharma; whoever sees the Dharma sees dependent origination."

quotes.text: 若見緣起便見法，若見法便見緣起。
quotes.note_en: If one sees dependent origination, one sees the Dharma; if one sees the Dharma, one sees dependent origination.

terms.root: saṃ-√sṛ「流動、漫遊」 · saṃ-√sṛ "to flow, wander on"
terms.short_zh: 有情因無明與愛，在三界六道中生死相續、流轉不已。
terms.short_en: Cyclic existence — beings wandering from birth to birth through the realms, driven by ignorance and craving.
terms.detail_zh:
saṃsāra 字面是「一同流動、漫遊」。《雜阿含經》：「於無始生死，無明所蓋，愛結所繫，長夜輪迴，不知苦之本際。」輪迴的動力是惑（無明、愛）與業；十二因緣正是輪迴的結構分析。

唯識以阿賴耶識的種子相續、「恒轉如瀑流」說明輪迴中沒有常一的我，卻有業果的延續。
terms.detail_en:
Saṃsāra literally means "flowing together, wandering on". Saṃyuktāgama: "Beings, in beginningless birth and death, covered by ignorance and bound by the fetter of craving, wander through the long night, not knowing the beginning of suffering." Its engine is affliction (ignorance, craving) and karma; the twelve links analyse its structure.

Yogācāra explains, through the continuity of seeds in the store consciousness "flowing like a torrent", how there is continuity of karma without a permanent self.

quotes.text: 於無始生死，無明所蓋，愛結所繫，長夜輪迴，不知苦之本際；
quotes.note_en: In beginningless birth and death, covered by ignorance and bound by the fetter of craving, [beings] wander on through the long night, not knowing the beginning of suffering.

terms.short_zh: 極長的時間單位，一個世界成住壞空的週期。
terms.short_en: Aeon — an immensely long unit of time; the cycle of a world's formation, duration, destruction and emptiness.
terms.detail_zh:
kalpa 是印度宇宙論的時間單位。《雜阿含經》以芥子喻形容其長：「譬如鐵城，方一由旬，高下亦爾，滿中芥子，有人百年取一芥子，盡其芥子，劫猶不竟。」

菩薩成佛需經「三大阿僧祇劫」（三無數劫），報身的功德就是在這樣長的時間中修集的。
terms.detail_en:
Kalpa is a unit of Indian cosmological time. The Saṃyuktāgama's mustard-seed simile: "Suppose an iron city a yojana on each side and as high, filled with mustard seeds; if someone removed one seed every hundred years, the seeds would be exhausted before the aeon ended."

A bodhisattva takes "three incalculable aeons" to become a buddha; the enjoyment body's qualities are gathered over such spans.

quotes.text: 譬如鐵城，方一由旬，高下亦爾，滿中芥子，有人百年取一芥子，盡其芥子，劫猶不竟。
quotes.note_en: Suppose an iron city one yojana square and as high, filled with mustard seeds; if someone took away one seed every hundred years, the seeds would be used up and still the aeon would not be over.

terms.root: ā-√yat「安住之處、進入之門」 · ā-√yat "to settle in": abode, entrance
terms.short_zh: 「諸識生長門」：六根與六境合為十二處，是識生起的門戶。舊譯「入」。
terms.short_en: "The gateway where consciousness grows": the six faculties and six objects form the twelve bases through which consciousness arises. Old translation 入.
terms.detail_zh:
《大乘五蘊論》：「以何義故名為處耶？諸識生長門義，是處義。」十二處是眼、耳、鼻、舌、身、意六內處（六根）與色、聲、香、味、觸、法六外處（六境）。識依根緣境而生，根與境就是識生長的「門」。舊譯「入」「入處」即取門戶之義。

**一切法**：《雜阿含經》第319經，有婆羅門問佛「一切」是什麼，佛答：「一切者，謂十二入處……是名一切。」除此之外說有別的「一切」，只是言說而已。

**意處與法處**：五蘊論說「意處即是識蘊」；「法處謂受想行蘊、無表色等及與無為」——所以十二處涵蓋有為與無為的一切法，比五蘊（只攝有為）更廣。
terms.detail_en:
Pañcaskandhaka: "In what sense is it called a base? In the sense of a gateway where consciousnesses grow." The twelve bases are the six internal (faculties: eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, mind) and six external (objects: visible form, sound, smell, taste, tangible, mental objects). Consciousness arises dependent on faculty and object — these are its "gates". The old rendering 入 "entrance" keeps this sense.

**"The All"**: in Saṃyuktāgama 319 a brahmin asks what "all" is; the Buddha answers: "All is the twelve bases … this is called all." To speak of any other "all" is mere words.

**Mind base and dharma base**: the Pañcaskandhaka says "the mind base is the consciousness aggregate" and "the dharma base is feeling, perception, formations, unmanifest form, etc., and the unconditioned" — so the twelve bases cover all dharmas, conditioned and unconditioned, wider than the aggregates (which cover only the conditioned).

quotes.text: 以何義故名為處耶？』答：『諸識生長門義，是處義。
quotes.note_en: In what sense is it called a base? In the sense of a gateway where consciousnesses grow — that is the meaning of base.

quotes.text: 一切者，謂十二入處，眼色、耳聲、鼻香、舌味、身觸、意法，是名一切。
quotes.note_en: "All" means the twelve bases: eye and forms, ear and sounds, nose and smells, tongue and tastes, body and tangibles, mind and mental objects — this is called all.

terms.short_zh: 「任持自相」之義：六根、六境、六識合為十八界，各持自己的特性，互不混雜。
terms.short_en: "Holding its own characteristic": the six faculties, six objects and six consciousnesses make the eighteen elements, each keeping its own nature.
terms.detail_zh:
十八界＝六根（眼界至意界）＋六境（色界至法界）＋六識（眼識界至意識界）。《大乘五蘊論》：「以能任持無作用性自相義故，說名為界。」每一界各自保持其特性，說明認識過程中沒有一個作用的「我」。說一切有部則以「種族」義解釋界（《俱舍論》：「聚、生門、種族，是蘊、處、界義」）。

**意界與意識界**：兩者看似重複，五蘊論說明：「言意界者，謂即彼無間滅等，為欲顯示第六意識，及廣建立十八界故」——前一剎那剛滅的識作為後一識的所依，稱為意界。

佛為何說蘊、處、界三科？五蘊論說：「為欲對治三種我執」——一性我執、受者我執、作者我執（見比較卡）。
terms.detail_en:
The eighteen elements = six faculties (eye element … mind element) + six objects (form element … dharma element) + six consciousnesses (eye-consciousness element … mind-consciousness element). Pañcaskandhaka: "It is called an element because it holds its own characteristic, being without agency." Each element keeps its nature, showing that no acting "self" is found in cognition. The Sarvāstivāda glosses dhātu as "lineage" (Abhidharmakośa: "heap, gateway of arising, lineage — the meanings of aggregate, base, element").

**Mind element vs mind-consciousness element**: they look redundant; the Pañcaskandhaka explains that "the mind element is [consciousness] that has just ceased, [named] to show the sixth consciousness and to establish the eighteen elements fully" — the immediately preceding moment of consciousness serving as support for the next.

Why three schemes — aggregates, bases, elements? "To counteract three kinds of self-grasping": grasping a unitary self, an experiencer, and an agent (see the comparison card).

quotes.text: 復有十八界，謂眼界、色界、眼識界，耳界、聲界、耳識界，鼻界、香界、鼻識界，舌界、味界、舌識界，身界、觸界、身識界，意界、法界、意識界。
quotes.note_en: There are also the eighteen elements — the eye element, form element, eye-consciousness element; ear, sound, ear-consciousness; nose, smell, nose-consciousness; tongue, taste, tongue-consciousness; body, tangible, body-consciousness; mind, mental-object, mind-consciousness elements.

quotes.text: 以何義故說名為界。
quotes.note_en: In what sense is it called an element? It is called an element because it holds its own characteristic, being without agency.

terms.root: indra「帝釋、主宰」→「主宰力」 · from Indra: "belonging to the ruler", controlling power
terms.short_zh: 具有「增上」主宰力的法；眼等六根對所生之識有主導作用。
terms.short_en: A faculty with governing power; the six sense faculties govern the consciousnesses they give rise to.
terms.detail_zh:
indriya 源自天神 Indra（帝釋），意為「主宰者的力量」。《俱舍論》：「最勝自在光顯名根，由此總成根增上義。」根是對某事有特殊主導力（增上）的法。

**眼等五根**不是肉眼可見的眼球等器官（稱「扶塵根」），而是「清淨色」（淨色根）——微細的感官能力。《大乘五蘊論》：「云何眼根？謂色為境清淨色。」

根的範圍不只六根。《俱舍論》列二十二根：眼等六根、男女二根、命根、苦樂憂喜捨五受根、信等五根（信、精進、念、定、慧）、三無漏根。五根五力中的「根」也是這個意思。
terms.detail_en:
Indriya derives from the god Indra: "power of a ruler". Abhidharmakośa: "Being foremost, sovereign and manifest is called faculty; hence the general meaning of faculty is dominance." A faculty is a dharma exercising special governing power over something.

**The five sense faculties** are not the visible eyeball etc. (the "supporting" organs) but "clear matter" — subtle sensory capacities. Pañcaskandhaka: "What is the eye faculty? Clear matter whose object is visible form."

Faculties are more than the six. The Abhidharmakośa lists twenty-two: the six sense faculties, male and female, life, the five feeling faculties (pain, pleasure, displeasure, joy, equanimity), the five faculties of faith, effort, mindfulness, concentration and wisdom, and three pure faculties. The "five faculties and powers" of practice use the same word.

quotes.text: 最勝自在光顯名根，由此總成根增上義。
quotes.note_en: Being foremost, sovereign and manifest is called faculty; hence altogether the meaning of faculty is dominance.

quotes.text: 云何眼根？謂色為境清淨色。
quotes.note_en: What is the eye faculty? Clear matter whose object is visible form.

terms.short_zh: 根所對、識所緣的對象：色、聲、香、味、觸、法六境。舊譯「塵」。
terms.short_en: The object a faculty engages and a consciousness cognizes — the six objects from visible form to mental objects. Old translation 塵 "dust".
terms.detail_zh:
viṣaya 原義是「範圍、領域」——根所能作用的範圍。六境（色、聲、香、味、觸、法）與六根相對，是識生起的外緣。《大乘五蘊論》逐一說明：色是「眼境界」，聲是「耳境界」……

**「塵」與「境」**：舊譯常作「六塵」，取其能染污心識、如塵垢之義；新譯作「六境」，較中性。

**所緣與境**：「境」側重對象對根而言的範圍；「所緣」（ālambana）側重心識攀緣的對象。在唯識學中，識所緣的「境」其實是識自身所變現的相分——「唯識無境」的「境」就是指離識獨立的外境。
terms.detail_en:
Viṣaya originally means "range, domain" — the scope in which a faculty operates. The six objects (visible form, sound, smell, taste, tangible, mental objects) face the six faculties and are the external condition for consciousness. The Pañcaskandhaka explains each: form is "the domain of the eye", sound "the domain of the ear" …

**塵 vs 境**: older translations say 六塵 "six dusts", since objects soil the mind like dust; newer ones 六境 "six objects", more neutral.

**Object and cognitive object**: viṣaya stresses the range relative to the faculty; ālambana stresses what the mind takes hold of. In Yogācāra the cognized "object" is actually the image-aspect manifested by consciousness itself — the 境 of "consciousness only, no [external] object" means an object existing independently of consciousness.

quotes.text: 云何為色？謂眼境界，顯色、形色及表色等。
quotes.note_en: What is visible form? The domain of the eye — colour, shape, bodily expression and so on.

terms.short_zh: 眼根：以色為境的清淨色；眼識的所依。
terms.short_en: The eye faculty — clear matter whose object is visible form; the support of eye-consciousness.
terms.detail_zh:
《大乘五蘊論》：「云何眼根？謂色為境清淨色。」眼根不是眼球，而是眼球中能見的微細淨色。眼根、色境、眼識三者和合而有觸——眼根是眼識的「所依」，也決定眼識的名稱（依根得名，故稱「眼識」而非「色識」）。

在十二處為眼處，在十八界為眼界，在五蘊屬色蘊。
terms.detail_en:
Pañcaskandhaka: "What is the eye faculty? Clear matter whose object is visible form." It is not the eyeball but the subtle clear matter within it that sees. Eye faculty, visible object and eye-consciousness meet in contact; the faculty is the support of eye-consciousness and gives it its name ("eye-consciousness", not "form-consciousness", since consciousness is named after its faculty).

It is the eye base among the twelve, the eye element among the eighteen, and belongs to the form aggregate.

quotes.text: 云何眼根？謂色為境清淨色。
quotes.note_en: What is the eye faculty? Clear matter whose object is visible form.

terms.short_zh: 耳根：以聲為境的清淨色；耳識的所依。
terms.short_en: The ear faculty — clear matter whose object is sound; the support of ear-consciousness.
terms.detail_zh: 《大乘五蘊論》：「云何耳根？謂聲為境清淨色。」與眼根同樣是微細的淨色根。耳根、聲、耳識和合而有聞。
terms.detail_en: Pañcaskandhaka: "What is the ear faculty? Clear matter whose object is sound." Like the eye, a subtle faculty of clear matter; ear faculty, sound and ear-consciousness together make hearing.

quotes.text: 云何耳根？謂聲為境清淨色。
quotes.note_en: What is the ear faculty? Clear matter whose object is sound.

terms.short_zh: 鼻根：以香為境的清淨色；鼻識的所依。
terms.short_en: The nose faculty — clear matter whose object is smell; the support of nose-consciousness.
terms.detail_zh:
《大乘五蘊論》：「云何鼻根？謂香為境清淨色。」

值得注意：色界天人沒有段食，所以不起鼻識、舌識——五蘊論說十八界中色界繫者十四，「除香、味，鼻、舌識」。
terms.detail_en:
Pañcaskandhaka: "What is the nose faculty? Clear matter whose object is smell."

Note: beings of the form realm take no coarse food, so nose- and tongue-consciousness do not arise there — the Pañcaskandhaka says fourteen of the eighteen elements belong to the form realm, "excluding smell, taste, and nose- and tongue-consciousness".

quotes.text: 云何鼻根？謂香為境清淨色。
quotes.note_en: What is the nose faculty? Clear matter whose object is smell.

terms.short_zh: 舌根：以味為境的清淨色；舌識的所依。
terms.short_en: The tongue faculty — clear matter whose object is taste; the support of tongue-consciousness.
terms.detail_zh: 《大乘五蘊論》：「云何舌根？謂味為境清淨色。」五蘊論列六種味：甘、酢（酸）、醎（鹹）、辛、苦、淡。
terms.detail_en: Pañcaskandhaka: "What is the tongue faculty? Clear matter whose object is taste." It lists six tastes: sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter and bland.

quotes.text: 云何舌根？謂味為境清淨色。
quotes.note_en: What is the tongue faculty? Clear matter whose object is taste.

terms.short_zh: 身根：以所觸為境的清淨色，遍布全身；身識的所依。
terms.short_en: The body faculty — clear matter whose object is the tangible, spread through the whole body; the support of body-consciousness.
terms.detail_zh:
《大乘五蘊論》：「云何身根？謂所觸為境清淨色。」身根遍於全身，感知冷暖、滑澀、輕重等觸。

**「身」字多義**：身根（kāya-indriya）是感官；身業的「身」指身體行為；「身識」是依身根的識；經中「身證」的「身」又有「親身」之義。讀經時要看上下文。
terms.detail_en:
Pañcaskandhaka: "What is the body faculty? Clear matter whose object is the tangible." It pervades the whole body, sensing cold and warmth, smoothness and roughness, heaviness and lightness.

**Many senses of 身/kāya**: the body faculty is a sense faculty; in "bodily karma" it means physical action; body-consciousness is consciousness based on the body faculty; in "realizing with the body" it means "in person". Read the context.

quotes.text: 云何身根？謂所觸為境清淨色。
quotes.note_en: What is the body faculty? Clear matter whose object is the tangible.

terms.short_zh: 意根：第六意識的所依。有部以前一剎那剛滅的識為意；唯識以第七末那識為意根。
terms.short_en: The mental faculty — the support of the sixth, mental consciousness. For the Sarvāstivāda it is the consciousness just ceased; for Yogācāra it is the seventh consciousness, manas.
terms.detail_zh:
意根是第六意識的所依，但它不是色法，所以與眼等五根不同。各派對「意根是什麼」看法不同：

- **說一切有部**：《俱舍論》：「由即六識身，無間滅為意。」任何一識在剛滅去的下一剎那，成為後一識的所依，就叫意（意界）。
- **唯識**：意識需要一個恆常的「俱有依」，這就是第七末那識；所以唯識所說的意根即末那識。

**名稱陷阱**：「意」（manas）、「意識」（mano-vijñāna）、「末那識」（kliṣṭa-manas，音譯「末那」即 manas）三者極易混淆——詳見比較卡。
terms.detail_en:
The mental faculty is the support of the sixth consciousness, but it is not matter, unlike the five sense faculties. Schools differ on what it is:

- **Sarvāstivāda**: Abhidharmakośa: "Any of the six consciousnesses, having just ceased, is manas." Whatever consciousness has just passed becomes the support of the next — the mind element.
- **Yogācāra**: the mental consciousness needs a constant simultaneous support, which is the seventh consciousness; so the Yogācāra mental faculty is manas.

**Naming trap**: manas (意), mano-vijñāna (意識) and the seventh consciousness (末那識, 末那 being a transliteration of manas) are easily confused — see the comparison card.

quotes.text: 由即六識身，無間滅為意。
quotes.note_en: Any of the six bodies of consciousness, having just ceased, is manas.

quotes.text: 言意界者，謂即彼無間滅等，為欲顯示第六意識，及廣建立十八界故。
quotes.note_en: The mind element is [consciousness] that has just ceased, etc.; [it is named] in order to show the sixth, mental consciousness and to establish the eighteen elements fully.

terms.short_zh: 眼所見的對象：顯色（青黃赤白等）、形色（長短方圓等）與表色。不同於作為五蘊之一的「色」。
terms.short_en: The object of the eye — colour, shape and bodily expression. Not the same as rūpa the aggregate.
terms.detail_zh:
《大乘五蘊論》：「云何為色？謂眼境界，顯色、形色及表色等。」顯色是青、黃、赤、白及光影明暗；形色是長、短、方、圓等；表色是身體動作所表現的形態。

**最重要的分辨**：同一個「色」字，作為**色蘊**是一切物質（包括五根、五境、無表色）；作為**色處／色境**只是眼所見的對象。所以「色處」只是「色蘊」中的一小部分。詳見比較卡「色蘊與色處」。

注意十八界的「色界」與三界的「色界」（rūpadhātu，色界天）也是完全不同的東西。
terms.detail_en:
Pañcaskandhaka: "What is visible form? The domain of the eye — colour, shape, bodily expression and so on." Colour is blue, yellow, red, white, light and shade; shape is long, short, square, round; expression is the configuration shown by bodily action.

**The key distinction**: the same word rūpa as the **form aggregate** means all matter (the five faculties, five objects, unmanifest form); as the **visible-form base** it means only what the eye sees. The visible-form base is a small part of the form aggregate. See the comparison card.

Note also that the "form element" (色界) of the eighteen elements has nothing to do with the "form realm" (rūpadhātu) of the three realms.

quotes.text: 云何為色？謂眼境界，顯色、形色及表色等。
quotes.note_en: What is visible form? The domain of the eye — colour, shape, bodily expression and so on.

terms.short_zh: 耳所聞的對象。依發聲的四大是否為有情所執受，分三類。
terms.short_en: The object of the ear, classed by whether the elements producing it are appropriated by a sentient being.
terms.detail_zh:
《大乘五蘊論》：「云何為聲？謂耳境界，執受大種因聲，非執受大種因聲，俱大種因聲。」執受大種因聲是有情身體發出的聲音（如說話），非執受大種因聲是無情物的聲音（如風、水），俱大種因聲是兩者共同產生的（如擊鼓）。

śabda 也有「語詞」之義——印度哲學中聲常住論（聲是永恆的）是佛教所批判的觀點之一。
terms.detail_en:
Pañcaskandhaka: "What is sound? The domain of the ear — sound caused by appropriated elements, by unappropriated elements, and by both." Appropriated: produced by a living body (speech); unappropriated: by insentient things (wind, water); both: e.g. a hand striking a drum.

Śabda also means "word"; the Indian doctrine that sound (the Vedic word) is eternal is one of the views Buddhism criticizes.

quotes.text: 云何為聲？謂耳境界，執受大種因聲，非執受大種因聲，俱大種因聲。
quotes.note_en: What is sound? The domain of the ear — sound caused by appropriated great elements, sound caused by unappropriated great elements, and sound caused by both.

terms.short_zh: 鼻所嗅的對象：好香、惡香及其餘之香。
terms.short_en: The object of the nose — pleasant, unpleasant and other smells.
terms.detail_zh: 《大乘五蘊論》：「云何為香？謂鼻境界，好香、惡香、及所餘香。」漢譯的「香」泛指一切氣味，不單指香氣，臭味也是「香境」。
terms.detail_en: Pañcaskandhaka: "What is smell? The domain of the nose — pleasant smells, unpleasant smells and other smells." Chinese 香 here covers all odours, not just fragrance; a stench is also a "香境".

quotes.text: 云何為香？謂鼻境界，好香、惡香、及所餘香。
quotes.note_en: What is smell? The domain of the nose — pleasant, unpleasant and other smells.

terms.short_zh: 舌所嘗的對象：甘、酢、醎、辛、苦、淡六味。
terms.short_en: The object of the tongue — sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter and bland.
terms.detail_zh:
《大乘五蘊論》：「云何為味？謂舌境界，甘味、酢味、醎味、辛味、苦味、淡味。」

rasa 在印度美學中也指「情味」（藝術感受）；在佛典中也常比喻法的滋味——「法味」「解脫味」，如南傳《增支部》（AN 8.19）說：大海唯一鹹味，此法與律唯一解脫味。
terms.detail_en:
Pañcaskandhaka: "What is taste? The domain of the tongue — sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter and bland."

Rasa is also "aesthetic flavour" in Indian poetics, and in the sūtras a metaphor for the taste of the Dharma — as the ocean has one taste, salt, so this Dharma and discipline has one taste, liberation (Aṅguttara Nikāya 8.19).

quotes.text: 云何為味？謂舌境界，甘味、酢味、醎味、辛味、苦味、淡味。
quotes.note_en: What is taste? The domain of the tongue — sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter and bland tastes.

terms.root: √spṛś 的未來被動分詞「應被觸的」 · gerundive of √spṛś, "to be touched"
terms.short_zh: 身所觸的對象：四大種及滑、澀、重、輕、冷、飢、渴等。注意與心所「觸」（sparśa）不同。
terms.short_en: The object of the body — the four elements and smoothness, roughness, heaviness, lightness, cold, hunger, thirst. Not the mental factor contact (sparśa).
terms.detail_zh:
《大乘五蘊論》：「云何為所觸一分？謂身境界，除四大種餘所造觸，滑性、澁性、重性、輕性、冷、飢、渴等。」又說「言觸處者，謂四大種及前所說所觸一分」——觸處包括能造的四大本身（堅、濕、煖、動）與所造觸。

**易混淆**：漢譯都作「觸」，但**觸境**（spraṣṭavya，「所觸」）是色法，是身根的對象；**觸心所**（sparśa）是遍行心所，是根境識三和合。兩者一屬色蘊，一屬行蘊（見比較卡）。
terms.detail_en:
Pañcaskandhaka: "What is part of the tangible? The domain of the body — derived tangibles other than the four elements: smoothness, roughness, heaviness, lightness, cold, hunger, thirst and so on." And: "the tangible base is the four elements and the part of the tangible just described" — it includes the elements themselves (solidity, cohesion, heat, motion) and derived tangibles.

**Easily confused**: Chinese uses 觸 for both, but the **tangible** (spraṣṭavya, "what is to be touched") is matter, the object of the body faculty; **contact** (sparśa) is an omnipresent mental factor, the meeting of faculty, object and consciousness. One is in the form aggregate, the other in formations (see the comparison card).

quotes.text: 云何為所觸一分？謂身境界，除四大種餘所造觸，滑性、澁性、重性、輕性、冷、飢、渴等。
quotes.note_en: What is part of the tangible? The domain of the body — derived tangibles other than the four great elements: smoothness, roughness, heaviness, lightness, cold, hunger, thirst and so on.

quotes.text: 言觸處者，謂四大種及前所說所觸一分。
quotes.note_en: The tangible base means the four great elements and the part of the tangible described before.

terms.short_zh: 意所緣的對象：受、想、行三蘊、無表色與無為法等，五根五境以外的一切法。
terms.short_en: The object of the mind — feeling, perception, formations, unmanifest form, the unconditioned: every dharma outside the five faculties and five objects.
terms.detail_zh:
《大乘五蘊論》：「言法處者，謂受想行蘊、無表色等及與無為。」法處是「剩餘」的一類：凡不屬於眼等五根、色等五境、意（識蘊）的一切法，都歸入法處——包括心所、心不相應行、無表色，以及虛空、擇滅、非擇滅、真如等無為法。

**「法」字的陷阱**：法處的「法」只是十二處之一；「一切法」的「法」卻是十二處全部。作為十八界之一的「法界」也不同於華嚴等所說的「法界」（dharmadhātu，真如法界）。
terms.detail_en:
Pañcaskandhaka: "The dharma base is the feeling, perception and formations aggregates, unmanifest form and so on, and the unconditioned." It is the "remainder" category: every dharma not among the five sense faculties, five objects or mind (the consciousness aggregate) — mental factors, non-associated formations, unmanifest form, and the unconditioned (space, the two cessations, suchness).

**The 法 trap**: the dharma of "dharma base" is one of twelve bases; the dharma of "all dharmas" is all twelve. And the "dharma element" among the eighteen is different from the Huayan "dharma-realm" (dharmadhātu, suchness).

quotes.text: 言法處者，謂受想行蘊無表色等及與無為。
quotes.note_en: The dharma base means the feeling, perception and formations aggregates, unmanifest form, etc., and the unconditioned.

terms.root: a-「非」＋ nitya「常」 · a- + nitya "constant, eternal"
terms.short_zh: 一切有為法剎那生滅、不常住。三法印之一。
terms.short_en: Impermanence — every conditioned thing arises and ceases moment by moment. One of the three seals.
terms.detail_zh:
有為法依因緣而生，因緣變則法變，所以沒有任何有為法能恆常不變。《大智度論》說佛法印第一即「一切有為法念念生滅皆無常」。

**觀無常是修行的起點**。《雜阿含經》第一經：「當觀色無常。如是觀者，則為正觀。正觀者，則生厭離；厭離者，喜貪盡；喜貪盡者，說心解脫。」

**無常→苦→無我**：經中常見的推理是「色無常，無常即苦，苦即非我」。注意三法印說「諸**行**無常」而說「諸**法**無我」：無常只就有為法說，涅槃是無為，不是無常。
terms.detail_en:
Conditioned dharmas arise from causes and conditions; when those change, the dharma changes, so nothing conditioned stays constant. The Dazhidu lun gives the first seal as "all conditioned dharmas arise and cease moment by moment — all are impermanent".

**Contemplating impermanence starts the path.** Saṃyuktāgama sūtra 1: "Contemplate form as impermanent. Seeing thus is right seeing. Right seeing gives rise to disenchantment; with disenchantment, delight and lust end; with their ending, the mind is said to be liberated."

**Impermanent → suffering → non-self**: the classic reasoning is "form is impermanent; what is impermanent is suffering; what is suffering is not self". Note the seals say "all *saṃskāras* are impermanent" but "all *dharmas* are non-self": impermanence applies only to the conditioned; nirvāṇa is unconditioned and not impermanent.

quotes.text: 當觀色無常。如是觀者，則為正觀。正觀者，則生厭離；厭離者，喜貪盡；喜貪盡者，說心解脫。
quotes.note_en: Contemplate form as impermanent. One who contemplates thus contemplates rightly. Right contemplation gives rise to disenchantment; disenchantment ends delight and lust; when delight and lust end, the mind is said to be liberated.

quotes.text: 何等是佛法印？答曰：佛法印有三種：一者、一切有為法念念生滅皆無常，二者、一切法無我，三者、寂滅涅槃。
quotes.note_en: What are the seals of the Buddha's Dharma? There are three — first, all conditioned dharmas arise and cease moment by moment and are all impermanent; second, all dharmas are non-self; third, nirvāṇa is peace.

terms.short_zh: 一切法中都沒有常、一、主宰的「我」。三法印之一，佛法的核心見地。
terms.short_en: Non-self — in no dharma is there a permanent, unitary, controlling self. One of the three seals, the core insight of Buddhism.
terms.detail_zh:
ātman 在印度哲學中指常住、單一、能主宰的自我。佛陀分析身心為五蘊、十二處、十八界，指出其中找不到這樣的「我」。《雜阿含經》第9經：「色無常，無常即苦，苦即非我，非我者亦非我所。」

**無我不是「沒有人」**：無我否定的是常一主宰的實體，並不否定因緣相續的生命之流、業果與責任。

**二無我**：大乘進一步說「人無我」（補特伽羅無我）與「法無我」——不但沒有實在的人我，一切法也沒有獨立的自性。
terms.detail_en:
In Indian philosophy ātman is a permanent, single, sovereign self. Analysing body and mind into aggregates, bases and elements, the Buddha shows no such self can be found. Saṃyuktāgama 9: "Form is impermanent; what is impermanent is suffering; what is suffering is not self; what is not self is not mine."

**Non-self is not "nobody"**: it denies a permanent controlling entity, not the conditioned stream of life, karma and responsibility.

**Twofold non-self**: the Mahāyāna adds that not only persons (pudgala-nairātmya) but all dharmas (dharma-nairātmya) lack intrinsic nature.

quotes.text: 色無常，無常即苦，苦即非我，非我者亦非我所。
quotes.note_en: Form is impermanent; what is impermanent is suffering; what is suffering is not self; what is not self is not mine either.

quotes.text: 一切行無常，一切法無我，涅槃寂滅。
quotes.note_en: All saṃskāras are impermanent, all dharmas are non-self, nirvāṇa is peace.

terms.root: nis-√vā「吹熄」 · nis-√vā "to blow out, extinguish"
terms.short_zh: 貪、瞋、癡與一切煩惱永盡的寂滅境界；無為法。三法印之一。
terms.short_en: Nirvāṇa — the peace in which greed, hatred, delusion and all afflictions are extinguished for good; unconditioned. One of the three seals.
terms.detail_zh:
nirvāṇa 字面是「吹熄」，如燈火熄滅——煩惱之火熄滅。《雜阿含經》第490經：「貪欲永盡，瞋恚永盡，愚癡永盡，一切諸煩惱永盡，是名涅槃。」

涅槃是**無為法**，不是一個「去處」，而是煩惱與生死的止息。部派佛教分**有餘依涅槃**（煩惱已盡，身體仍在）與**無餘依涅槃**（身亦滅盡）。唯識另立「本來自性清淨涅槃」與「無住處涅槃」，合為四種涅槃。

《大般涅槃經》偈：「諸行無常，是生滅法；生滅滅已，寂滅為樂。」
terms.detail_en:
Nirvāṇa literally means "blowing out", like a lamp going out — the fire of affliction extinguished. Saṃyuktāgama 490: "Greed ended forever, hatred ended forever, delusion ended forever, all afflictions ended forever — this is called nirvāṇa."

Nirvāṇa is **unconditioned**: not a place one goes but the cessation of affliction and rebirth. The Abhidharma distinguishes nirvāṇa **with remainder** (afflictions ended, body still present) and **without remainder** (body also ended). Yogācāra adds "innately pure nirvāṇa" and "non-abiding nirvāṇa", four in all.

Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra verse: "All saṃskāras are impermanent, subject to arising and ceasing; when arising and ceasing have ceased, that stillness is bliss."

quotes.text: 貪欲永盡，瞋恚永盡，愚癡永盡，一切諸煩惱永盡，是名涅槃。
quotes.note_en: Greed ended forever, hatred ended forever, delusion ended forever, all afflictions ended forever — this is called nirvāṇa.

quotes.text: 生滅滅已，寂滅為樂。
quotes.note_en: When arising and ceasing have ceased, that stillness is bliss.

terms.short_zh: 防非止惡的品行與戒律；三學之首、六度之二，是定與慧的基礎。
terms.short_en: Morality — conduct and precepts that guard against wrongdoing; first of the three trainings, second perfection, the basis of concentration and wisdom.
terms.detail_zh:
śīla 原義是「習性、品行」，漢譯「戒」，音譯「尸羅」。戒不只是外在規條，更是養成的善良品格。

**三學的次第**：《雜阿含經》說「有三學……謂增上戒學、增上意學、增上慧學」。《楞嚴經》概括為：「攝心為戒，因戒生定，因定發慧。」沒有戒，心不能安定；心不安定，智慧無從生起。

**戒是解脫之本**：《遺教經》：「戒是正順解脫之本，故名波羅提木叉。」
terms.detail_en:
Śīla originally means "habit, character"; Chinese 戒 "precept", transliterated 尸羅. It is not just external rules but cultivated good character.

**The order of the three trainings**: the Saṃyuktāgama speaks of "three trainings — higher morality, higher mind and higher wisdom". The Śūraṅgama sums it up: "Gathering the mind is morality; from morality comes concentration; from concentration arises wisdom." Without morality the mind cannot settle; without a settled mind no wisdom arises.

**The root of liberation**: the Yijiao jing: "Morality is the foundation that accords with liberation; hence it is called prātimokṣa."

quotes.text: 有三學。何等為三？謂增上戒學、增上意學、謂增上慧學。
quotes.note_en: There are three trainings. What are the three? Higher morality, higher mind and higher wisdom.

quotes.text: 戒是正順解脫之本，故名波羅提木叉。
quotes.source_en: Sūtra of the Bequeathed Teaching (Yijiao jing)
quotes.note_en: Morality is the foundation that accords with liberation; hence it is called prātimokṣa.

terms.short_zh: 十二因緣第四支。「名」是受、想、行、識四無色蘊，「色」是四大及所造色；即身心的最初組合。
terms.short_en: The fourth link. "Name" is the four non-material aggregates, "form" the elements and derived matter — the first combination of mind and body.
terms.detail_zh:
《雜阿含經》第298經：「云何名？謂四無色陰——受陰、想陰、行陰、識陰。云何色？謂四大、四大所造色……此色及前所說名，是為名色。」所以名色就是**五蘊**的另一種說法，強調心（名）與物（色）的結合。

**分位緣起**：說一切有部把十二支解釋為一生中的不同階段。《俱舍論》：「識正結生蘊，六處前名色」——識支是投胎那一剎那的五蘊，此後到六根完備之前的胎中階段就是名色。

**識與名色相依**：《雜阿含經》第288經又以「三蘆立於空地，展轉相依，而得竪立」比喻識與名色互相依存——識依名色而住，名色依識而生長。
terms.detail_en:
Saṃyuktāgama 298: "What is name? The four non-material aggregates — feeling, perception, formations, consciousness. What is form? The four elements and derived form … This form together with the name just described is name-and-form." Name-and-form is thus the **five aggregates** seen as the union of mind (name) and matter (form).

**Phase interpretation**: the Sarvāstivāda reads the twelve links as stages of life. Abhidharmakośa: "consciousness is the aggregates at the moment of conception; name-and-form comes before the six bases" — the embryonic phase after conception until the sense faculties are complete.

**Mutual dependence**: Saṃyuktāgama 288 compares consciousness and name-and-form to "three reeds standing on open ground, leaning on one another, and so standing upright" — consciousness abides in name-and-form, name-and-form grows through consciousness.

quotes.text: 緣識名色者，云何名？謂四無色陰——受陰、想陰、行陰、識陰。云何色？謂四大、四大所造色，是名為色。此色及前所說名，是為名色。
quotes.note_en: "Consciousness conditions name-and-form" — what is name? The four non-material aggregates: feeling, perception, formations and consciousness. What is form? The four elements and form derived from them. This form and the name described before are called name-and-form.

quotes.text: 識正結生蘊，六處前名色
quotes.note_en: Consciousness is the aggregates at the very moment of conception; before the six bases [are formed] is name-and-form.

quotes.text: 三蘆立於空地，展轉相依，而得竪立
quotes.note_en: Like three reeds standing on open ground, leaning on one another, they are able to stand upright.

terms.root: ṣaṭ「六」＋ āyatana「處、入」 · ṣaṭ "six" + āyatana "base, entrance"
terms.short_zh: 十二因緣第五支：眼、耳、鼻、舌、身、意六內入處，是觸的所依。
terms.short_en: The fifth link — the six internal sense bases, eye to mind, the basis of contact.
terms.detail_zh:
《雜阿含經》第298經：「云何為六入處？謂六內入處——眼入處、耳入處、鼻入處、舌入處、身入處、意入處。」舊譯「六入」，新譯「六處」。在十二因緣中專指**內**六處（六根），不含外六境。

**分位緣起**：《俱舍論》：「從生眼等根，三和前六處」——胎中六根生起之後，到根、境、識三者能和合產生觸之前，這個階段叫六處。

六處是認識世界的「門」（āyatana 有「入口」之義），由此才有觸、受，進而生愛。
terms.detail_en:
Saṃyuktāgama 298: "What are the six sense bases? The six internal bases — eye, ear, nose, tongue, body and mind." Older translations say 六入 "six entrances", newer 六處. In the twelve links they are the **internal** six (the faculties), not the external objects.

**Phase interpretation**: Abhidharmakośa: "from the arising of the eye and other faculties until before the meeting of the three is the six bases" — after the faculties form in the womb, until faculty, object and consciousness can meet in contact.

The six bases are the "gates" to the world (āyatana also means "entrance"); through them come contact and feeling, and then craving.

quotes.text: 緣名色六入處者，云何為六入處？謂六內入處——眼入處、耳入處、鼻入處、舌入處、身入處、意入處。
quotes.note_en: "Name-and-form conditions the six sense bases" — what are the six sense bases? The six internal bases: the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body and mind bases.

quotes.text: 從生眼等根，三和前六處
quotes.note_en: From the arising of the eye and other faculties until before the meeting of the three is [the link of] the six bases.

terms.short_zh: 十二因緣第八支：由受而生的渴求。分欲愛、色愛、無色愛；也是四諦中苦的集因。
terms.short_en: The eighth link — thirst arising from feeling. Craving for the desire, form and formless realms; also the origin of suffering in the four truths.
terms.detail_zh:
tṛṣṇā 字面是「口渴」——像口渴的人求水一樣急切。《雜阿含經》第298經：「云何為愛？謂三愛——欲愛、色愛、無色愛。」南傳經典則常分為欲愛、有愛、無有愛（kāma-, bhava-, vibhava-taṇhā），這是四聖諦中「集諦」的內容。

**受緣愛**是十二因緣中最關鍵、也最可以用功的環節：受是過去業的果報，無法立即改變；但在受生起時不起愛，輪迴的鎖鏈就在這裡斷開。

**愛與貪**：愛是貪（rāga）在渴求上的表現。《俱舍論》以「貪資具婬愛」說明愛支：對欲樂資具與男女之愛的貪著。
terms.detail_en:
Tṛṣṇā literally means "thirst" — urgent like a parched man seeking water. Saṃyuktāgama 298: "What is craving? Three cravings — for the desire realm, the form realm and the formless realm." Pāli suttas often list craving for sense pleasures, for existence and for non-existence (kāma-, bhava-, vibhava-taṇhā), the content of the second noble truth.

**"Feeling conditions craving"** is the most crucial — and most workable — link: feeling is the result of past karma and cannot be changed at once; but if craving does not arise when feeling arises, the chain of saṃsāra breaks right here.

**Craving and greed**: craving is greed (rāga) in the mode of thirst. The Abhidharmakośa explains the link as "greed for the means of pleasure and sexual love".

quotes.text: 緣受愛者，彼云何為愛？謂三愛——欲愛、色愛、無色愛。
quotes.note_en: "Feeling conditions craving" — what is craving? The three cravings: craving for desire, for form, and for the formless.

quotes.text: 在婬愛前受，貪資具婬愛
quotes.note_en: Before sexual love is [the link of] feeling; greed for the means of pleasure and sexual love is craving.

terms.root: upa-ā-√dā「拿取、執持」 · upa-ā-√dā "to take up, seize"
terms.short_zh: 十二因緣第九支：愛增強而成的執取、四處追求。分欲取、見取、戒禁取、我語取。
terms.short_en: The ninth link — craving intensified into grasping and pursuit. Four kinds — sense pleasures, views, rules and rituals, self-doctrine.
terms.detail_zh:
upādāna 字面是「拿起來、抓住」，也有「燃料」的意思——取是輪迴之火的燃料。《雜阿含經》第298經：「云何為取？四取——欲取、見取、戒取、我取。」

**愛與取的不同**：愛是渴求，取是抓取。《俱舍論》：「為得諸境界，遍馳求名取」——愛漸增長，於是為了得到對象而四處奔走追求。四取之中，後三者都涉及「見」：執著見解、執著錯誤的戒律禁制、執著「我」的學說。

**五取蘊**：五蘊被稱為「取蘊」（upādāna-skandha），因為它們由取而生，又能生取。
terms.detail_en:
Upādāna literally means "taking up, seizing", and also "fuel" — clinging is the fuel of saṃsāra's fire. Saṃyuktāgama 298: "What is clinging? Four clingings — to sense pleasures, to views, to rules and rituals, and to self."

**Craving vs clinging**: craving is thirst, clinging is grabbing. Abhidharmakośa: "running about everywhere seeking to obtain objects is clinging" — as craving grows, one pursues its objects everywhere. Three of the four clingings concern views: clinging to opinions, to wrong observances, to doctrines of a self.

**Aggregates of clinging**: the aggregates are called "aggregates of clinging" (upādāna-skandha) because they arise from clinging and give rise to it.

quotes.text: 緣愛取者，云何為取？四取——欲取、見取、戒取、我取。
quotes.note_en: "Craving conditions clinging" — what is clinging? The four clingings: to sense pleasures, to views, to rules, and to self.

quotes.text: 為得諸境界，遍馳求名取
quotes.note_en: Running about everywhere seeking to obtain objects is called clinging.

terms.short_zh: 十二因緣第十支：能牽引來生的業力（業有），及其所招的三界存在（欲有、色有、無色有）。
terms.short_en: The tenth link — the karma that projects the next life, and the existence in the three realms it brings.
terms.detail_zh:
《雜阿含經》第298經：「云何為有？三有——欲有、色有、無色有。」有即三界的存在。

**有是業**：《俱舍論》解釋有支：「有謂正能造，牽當有果業」——因愛、取而造作的、能牽引未來果報的業，就是有。所以有支雖名為「存在」，實際著重在**業**：今生的愛、取、有是未來生的因。

**行與有**：兩者都是業，差別在時間：行是過去世的業（招感今生），有是今生的業（招感來生）。
terms.detail_en:
Saṃyuktāgama 298: "What is becoming? Three becomings — in the desire, form and formless realms." Bhava is existence in the three realms.

**Becoming is karma**: the Abhidharmakośa explains the link: "becoming means actually creating the karma that projects future existence" — karma done out of craving and clinging that pulls toward future results. Though named "existence", the link stresses **karma**: this life's craving, clinging and becoming are the causes of the next.

**Formations vs becoming**: both are karma; they differ in time — formations are past-life karma (bringing this life), becoming is present-life karma (bringing the next).

quotes.text: 緣取有者，云何為有？三有——欲有、色有、無色有。
quotes.note_en: "Clinging conditions becoming" — what is becoming? The three becomings: in the desire, form and formless realms.

quotes.text: 有謂正能造，牽當有果業
quotes.note_en: Becoming means actually creating the karma that projects the future existence.

terms.short_zh: 十二因緣第十一支：由有（業）而在來世出生，得五蘊、界、處、命根。
terms.short_en: The eleventh link — birth in a future life brought about by becoming, acquiring aggregates, elements, bases and life-faculty.
terms.detail_zh:
《雜阿含經》第298經：「云何為生？若彼彼眾生，彼彼身種類一生，超越和合出生，得陰、得界、得入處、得命根，是名為生。」生就是新的五蘊、十八界、十二處與命根的出現。

**分位緣起**：《俱舍論》：「結當有名生」——在未來世結生（投胎）的那一刻就是生支。依三世兩重因果，生與老死是「未來二果」。

注意：十二因緣的「生」（jāti）與心不相應行中作為有為相的「生」（生相）不同，後者指一切有為法剎那的生起。
terms.detail_en:
Saṃyuktāgama 298: "What is birth? For this or that being, in this or that class, being born, emerging, coming together, appearing, acquiring the aggregates, the elements, the sense bases and the life-faculty — this is birth." Birth is the appearance of a new set of aggregates, elements, bases and life-faculty.

**Phase interpretation**: Abhidharmakośa: "conception in the future existence is birth". In the scheme of "two layers of cause and effect over three lives", birth and ageing-and-death are the two future effects.

Note: the birth (jāti) of the twelve links differs from "arising" as a characteristic of conditioned things among the non-associated formations, which refers to the momentary arising of every conditioned dharma.

quotes.text: 緣有生者，云何為生？若彼彼眾生，彼彼身種類一生，超越和合出生，得陰、得界、得入處、得命根，是名為生。
quotes.note_en: "Becoming conditions birth" — what is birth? For this or that being, in this or that class, being born, emerging and coming forth, acquiring the aggregates, the elements, the sense bases and the life-faculty — this is called birth.

quotes.text: 結當有名生，至當受老死。
quotes.note_en: Conception into the future existence is birth; [from then] until the time of feeling [in that life] is ageing-and-death.

terms.root: jarā「衰老」＋ maraṇa「死」 · jarā "old age" + maraṇa "death"
terms.short_zh: 十二因緣最後一支：有生必有老死，以及隨之而來的憂悲苦惱。
terms.short_en: The last link — whatever is born must age and die, with the sorrow, lamentation, pain and despair that follow.
terms.detail_zh:
《雜阿含經》第298經生動地描寫老：「髮白露頂，皮緩根熟，支弱背僂……柱杖而行」；死則是「彼彼眾生，彼彼種類沒、遷移、身壞、壽盡、火離、命滅，捨陰時到，是名為死」。

老死是十二因緣的終點，也是佛陀出家的起點——四門遊觀所見的老、病、死，引發了尋求解脫之路。緣起的「流轉門」從無明推到老死；「還滅門」則從老死逆推回無明：要滅老死，就要滅生……直到滅無明。
terms.detail_en:
Saṃyuktāgama 298 describes ageing vividly: "hair white, head bald, skin slack, faculties ripe, limbs weak, back bent … walking with a stick"; and death: "the passing away of this or that being from this or that class, departing, break-up of the body, end of life-span, loss of heat, extinction of life, the time of abandoning the aggregates — this is death."

Ageing-and-death is the end of the twelve links — and the starting point of the Buddha's renunciation: seeing old age, sickness and death set him on the search for liberation. The "forward" order of dependent origination runs from ignorance to ageing-and-death; the "reverse" order traces back: to end ageing-and-death one must end birth … down to ending ignorance.

quotes.text: 云何為死？彼彼眾生，彼彼種類沒、遷移、身壞、壽盡、火離、命滅，捨陰時到，是名為死。此死及前說老，是名老死。
quotes.note_en: What is death? The passing away of this or that being from this or that class, departure, break-up of the body, end of the life-span, loss of heat, extinction of life, the time of abandoning the aggregates — this is death. This death and the ageing described before are called ageing-and-death.

terms.root: pari-√kḷp「周遍地構想」 · pari-√kḷp "to imagine all around"
terms.short_zh: 三自性之一：由周遍計度而執為實有的我與法——如誤認繩為蛇的「蛇」，本無實體。
terms.short_en: One of the three natures — self and dharmas that pervasive conceptualization grasps as real; like the "snake" seen in a rope, it has no existence.
terms.detail_zh:
《唯識三十頌》：「由彼彼遍計，遍計種種物，此遍計所執，自性無所有。」意識與末那識種種計度（遍計），把依他起的現象執為實在的「我」與「法」；這些被執著的實我、實法就是遍計所執性，**體性全無**。

**繩蛇喻**：昏暗中把繩子看成蛇——「蛇」是遍計所執（本無），「繩」是依他起（因緣所生，有而非實），繩的真實本性（麻）喻圓成實。

依此立「相無性」：遍計所執之相本來沒有。
terms.detail_en:
Thirty Verses: "Whatever is imagined by this or that imagining, of various things — this imagined nature has no existence." The sixth and seventh consciousnesses construct and cling (parikalpa), taking dependently arisen phenomena as a real self and real dharmas; that grasped self and those grasped dharmas are the imagined nature — **wholly non-existent**.

**Rope and snake**: in the dark one sees a rope as a snake — the snake is the imagined nature (non-existent), the rope the dependent nature (arisen from conditions, existent but not ultimately real), and the rope's true nature (hemp) the perfected nature.

On this basis the "non-nature of characteristics" is taught: the imagined characteristic simply is not.

quotes.text: 由彼彼遍計，遍計種種物，此遍計所執，自性無所有。依他起自性，分別緣所生。圓成實於彼，常遠離前性。
quotes.note_en: Whatever is imagined by this or that imagining, of various things — this imagined nature has no existence. The dependent nature arises from conceptualization and conditions. The perfected is that [dependent nature] forever free of the former [imagined nature].

terms.short_zh: 三自性之一：依因緣而生起的一切心、心所及其所變現——如幻而有，非實非無。
terms.short_en: One of the three natures — mind, mental factors and what they manifest, arising from conditions; existent like an illusion, neither real nor nothing.
terms.detail_zh:
《唯識三十頌》：「依他起自性，分別緣所生。」一切有為法都是依眾緣而生（「依他」而起），在唯識中特指八識心王、心所及其見分、相分。

依他起**有而不實**：它確實在因緣中生起（不同於遍計所執的全無），但沒有獨立的自性，如夢如幻。它是雜染與清淨的所依：執著它就成遍計所執，看透它就顯圓成實。

依此立「生無性」：依他起的法不是自然生，而是依緣而生，故無自生之性。
terms.detail_en:
Thirty Verses: "The dependent nature arises from conceptualization and conditions." All conditioned dharmas arise dependent on conditions; in Yogācāra it means specifically the eight consciousnesses, mental factors and their seeing and image aspects.

It **exists but is not real**: it truly arises from conditions (unlike the utterly non-existent imagined nature) yet has no independent nature, like a dream or illusion. It is the basis of both defilement and purity: clung to, it becomes the imagined; seen through, it reveals the perfected.

On this basis the "non-nature of arising" is taught: dependent dharmas do not arise by themselves.

quotes.text: 由彼彼遍計，遍計種種物，此遍計所執，自性無所有。依他起自性，分別緣所生。圓成實於彼，常遠離前性。
quotes.note_en: Whatever is imagined by this or that imagining — this imagined nature has no existence. The dependent nature arises from conceptualization and conditions. The perfected is that [dependent nature] forever free of the former.

terms.root: pari-niṣ-√pad「圓滿成就」 · pari-niṣ-√pad "to be fully accomplished"
terms.short_zh: 三自性之一：依他起上遠離遍計所執所顯的真實本性，即真如；圓滿、成就、真實。
terms.short_en: One of the three natures — the true nature revealed when the dependent is free of the imagined; suchness — perfect, accomplished, real.
terms.detail_zh:
《唯識三十頌》：「圓成實於彼，常遠離前性。」圓成實性不是在依他起之外另有一物，而是依他起「遠離遍計所執」之後所顯的真實——即我空、法空所顯的真如。

成唯識論解釋其名：「圓滿、成就、諸法實性」——遍一切法（圓）、不生不滅（成）、非虛妄（實）。

依此立「勝義無性」：圓成實是遠離一切執著的勝義，無我法之性。
terms.detail_en:
Thirty Verses: "The perfected is that [dependent nature] forever free of the former." It is not something apart from the dependent nature but the reality that appears when the dependent is free of the imagined — the suchness disclosed by emptiness of self and dharmas.

The Cheng weishi lun glosses the name as "complete, accomplished, the real nature of dharmas": pervading all dharmas, neither arising nor ceasing, not false.

On this basis the "ultimate non-nature" is taught: the perfected is the ultimate, free of all grasping at self and dharmas.

quotes.text: 真謂真實，顯非虛妄，如謂如常，表無變易
quotes.note_en: "True" means real, showing it is not false; "such" means constantly so, indicating that it does not change.

terms.root: niḥ「無」＋ sva-bhāva「自有的存在」 · niḥ "without" + svabhāva "own-being"
terms.short_zh: 一切法沒有獨立、固定的自性。唯識依三自性立相無性、生無性、勝義無性三無性。
terms.short_en: Dharmas lack independent, fixed own-being. Yogācāra bases three non-natures — of characteristics, arising and the ultimate — on the three natures.
terms.detail_zh:
svabhāva（自性）指法自身固有、不依他的本質。般若、中觀說「一切法無自性」，因為一切法都依緣而起。

唯識學認為「一切法無性」是佛的**密意說**：《唯識三十頌》：「即依此三性，立彼三無性，故佛密意說，一切法無性。」遍計所執是**相無性**（相本無），依他起是**生無性**（非自然生），圓成實是**勝義無性**（遠離我法之性）。並非說一切都不存在。
terms.detail_en:
Svabhāva ("own-being") is a dharma's intrinsic, independent essence. Prajñāpāramitā and Madhyamaka teach that all dharmas lack it, because all arise dependently.

Yogācāra reads "all dharmas are without nature" as the Buddha's **intended meaning**: Thirty Verses: "Based on these three natures the three non-natures are established; thus the Buddha, with a hidden intention, taught that all dharmas are without nature." The imagined lacks characteristics, the dependent lacks self-arising, the perfected is the ultimate free of self and dharmas. It does not mean that nothing exists.

quotes.text: 即依此三性，立彼三無性，故佛密意說，一切法無性。
quotes.note_en: Based on these three natures the three non-natures are established; therefore the Buddha, with a hidden intention, taught that all dharmas are without nature.

terms.short_zh: 阿賴耶識中能親生自果的功能；現行熏成種子，種子又生現行。
terms.short_en: Seed — the potential in the store consciousness that directly produces its own result; actions imprint seeds, seeds produce actions.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「何法名為種子？謂本識中親生自果，功能差別。」種子不是物質的顆粒，而是潛藏在阿賴耶識中、能生起相應現象的潛能。

**種子與現行**：「種子生現行，現行熏種子」——心識活動（現行）在阿賴耶識留下印記（熏習成種子），種子遇緣又生起新的現行，構成業力相續、輪迴不斷的機制。

**種子六義**：《攝大乘論》：「剎那滅、俱有、恒隨轉應知、決定、待眾緣、唯能引自果。」
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "What is called a seed? The particular potency in the root consciousness that directly produces its own result." A seed is not a physical particle but a latent capacity in the store consciousness to give rise to corresponding phenomena.

**Seeds and manifestation**: "seeds produce manifestation, manifestation imprints seeds" — mental activity leaves traces in the store consciousness (perfuming, forming seeds), and seeds meeting conditions produce new activity: the mechanism of karmic continuity and rebirth.

**Six characteristics of seeds** (Mahāyānasaṃgraha): "momentary, simultaneous [with the result], continuous, determinate, dependent on conditions, producing only their own result."

quotes.text: 何法名為種子？謂本識中親生自果，功能差別。
quotes.note_en: What dharma is called a seed? The particular potency in the root consciousness that directly produces its own result.

quotes.text: 剎那滅、俱有，恒隨轉應知、決定、待眾緣、唯能引自果。
quotes.note_en: Momentary, simultaneous, continuously following — know this — determinate, dependent on conditions, and able to produce only their own result.

terms.short_zh: 如香熏衣般在心識中留下的餘勢；唯識中常作種子的異名。
terms.short_en: Habitual tendency — residual force left in the mind as scent lingers in cloth; in Yogācāra often another name for seeds.
terms.detail_zh:
vāsanā 原義是「熏香」：衣服放在香旁，香氣便沾染在衣上。心識的活動也會在阿賴耶識中留下這樣的「氣分」，稱為習氣，也就是種子。

《唯識三十頌》：「由諸業習氣，二取習氣俱，前異熟既盡，復生餘異熟。」業習氣（善惡業種子）決定來生的果報，二取習氣（能取、所取的名言種子）提供生起的材料——兩者合作使生死相續。

**斷煩惱與斷習氣**：阿羅漢斷盡煩惱，但佛才能連習氣也斷盡（《大智度論》卷26舉阿羅漢摩頭波斯咤仍跳上梁棚、畢陵伽婆蹉罵恒河神「小婢」為例）。
terms.detail_en:
Vāsanā originally means "perfuming": cloth kept near incense takes on its scent. Mental activity likewise leaves such "scent" in the store consciousness — habitual tendencies, i.e. seeds.

Thirty Verses: "Through the habitual tendencies of karma, together with the tendencies of the twofold grasping, when the former maturation is exhausted, another maturation arises." Karmic tendencies decide the next life's results; tendencies of grasper and grasped supply the material — together they sustain rebirth.

**Afflictions vs tendencies**: arhats end the afflictions, but only a buddha removes even the residual tendencies (the Dazhidu lun, fasc. 26, cites an arhat who still leapt onto beams like a monkey, and Pilindavatsa calling the Ganges deity "little maid").

quotes.text: 由諸業習氣、二取習氣俱，前異熟既盡，復生餘異熟。
quotes.note_en: Because of the habitual tendencies of karma together with the tendencies of the twofold grasping, when the former maturation is exhausted, another maturation arises.

terms.root: vijñapti「表象、了別」＋ mātra「唯」 · vijñapti "representation" + mātra "only"
terms.short_zh: 一切所認識的對象都是識所變現，離識之外沒有實在的外境。
terms.short_en: Consciousness-only — everything cognized is a manifestation of consciousness; there is no real object apart from it.
terms.detail_zh:
《唯識三十頌》：「是諸識轉變，分別、所分別，由此彼皆無，故一切唯識。」諸識轉變，現出能分別的見分與所分別的相分；在此之外，所執的實我、實法都不存在。

**「唯識」不是唯我論**：唯識並不否認他人與世界的存在，而是說：我們所經驗的一切，都是透過識變現而呈現的；執著有離識獨立的外境，正是遍計所執。唯識也不把識執為實有——「若執唯識真實有者，如執外境，亦是法執」。
terms.detail_en:
Thirty Verses: "These transformations of consciousness are the discriminating and the discriminated; hence neither [self nor dharmas] exists — therefore all is consciousness-only." Consciousness transforms into a seeing aspect and an image aspect; beyond them the real self and dharmas one clings to do not exist.

**Not solipsism**: consciousness-only does not deny other beings or the world; it says that everything we experience appears through consciousness's manifestation, and that grasping at objects independent of consciousness is the imagined nature. Nor does it make consciousness itself absolutely real — clinging to "consciousness-only" as truly existent is also clinging to dharmas.

quotes.text: 是諸識轉變，分別、所分別，由此彼皆無，故一切唯識。
quotes.note_en: These transformations of consciousness are the discriminating and the discriminated; because of this, those [self and dharmas] do not exist; therefore everything is consciousness-only.

terms.root: āśraya「所依」＋ parā-√vṛt「翻轉」 · āśraya "basis" + parāvṛtti "turning around"
terms.short_zh: 修道的最終成果：轉捨依他起上的遍計所執與雜染，轉得圓成實的菩提與涅槃；轉八識成四智。
terms.short_en: The goal of the path — discarding defilement and the imagined on the dependent basis and attaining awakening and nirvāṇa; the eight consciousnesses become the four wisdoms.
terms.detail_zh:
「依」是所依——依他起性（也指阿賴耶識）；「轉」是轉捨與轉得。《唯識三十頌》：「無得不思議，是出世間智，捨二麁重故，便證得轉依。」捨去煩惱障與所知障的「二麁重」，證得轉依。

**二轉依果**：斷煩惱障得大涅槃，斷所知障得大菩提。

**轉識成智**：前五識轉成所作智、第六意識轉妙觀察智、第七末那轉平等性智、第八阿賴耶轉大圓鏡智。
terms.detail_en:
The "basis" is the dependent nature (also the store consciousness); "transformation" is discarding and attaining. Thirty Verses: "Non-apprehending and inconceivable, this is transcendent wisdom; by discarding the twofold heaviness, the transformation of the basis is realized." Discarding the "twofold heaviness" — the obstructions of affliction and of the knowable — one realizes it.

**Two fruits**: ending the afflictive obstruction yields great nirvāṇa; ending the cognitive obstruction yields great awakening.

**Consciousness into wisdom**: the five sense consciousnesses become the wisdom that accomplishes tasks, the sixth the wisdom of wondrous observation, the seventh the wisdom of equality, the eighth mirror-like wisdom.

quotes.text: 無得不思議，是出世間智，捨二麁重故，便證得轉依。
quotes.note_en: Without apprehension and inconceivable, this is transcendent wisdom; by discarding the twofold heaviness, the transformation of the basis is realized.

terms.root: kleśa「煩惱」＋ āvaraṇa「障、覆蓋」 · kleśa "affliction" + āvaraṇa "covering"
terms.short_zh: 以我執為根本的煩惱，擾亂身心、障礙涅槃；斷之證真解脫。
terms.short_en: The afflictive obstruction — afflictions rooted in self-grasping that disturb body and mind and block nirvāṇa; ending it brings true liberation.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》開宗明義：「由我、法執二障具生，若證二空，彼障隨斷。斷障為得二勝果故，由斷續生煩惱障故，證真解脫；由斷礙解所知障故，得大菩提。」

煩惱障由**我執**而生，以身見為首的根本、隨煩惱，使眾生相續受生、身心擾惱，障礙涅槃。聲聞、緣覺斷煩惱障而證解脫；菩薩兼斷所知障而成佛。
terms.detail_en:
The Cheng weishi lun opens: "From grasping at self and dharmas the two obstructions arise; realizing the two emptinesses, they are removed. The obstructions are cut to gain two supreme fruits: cutting the afflictive obstruction that continues rebirth, one realizes true liberation; cutting the cognitive obstruction that hinders understanding, one attains great awakening."

The afflictive obstruction arises from **self-grasping**: root and secondary afflictions headed by self-view, which keep beings taking rebirth and disturb body and mind, blocking nirvāṇa. Disciples and pratyekabuddhas end it and attain liberation; bodhisattvas also end the cognitive obstruction and become buddhas.

quotes.text: 由我、法執二障具生，若證二空，彼障隨斷。斷障為得二勝果故，由斷續生煩惱障故，證真解脫；由斷礙解所知障故，得大菩提。
quotes.note_en: From grasping at self and at dharmas the two obstructions arise; when the two emptinesses are realized, these obstructions are removed accordingly. The obstructions are cut to gain two supreme fruits — by cutting the afflictive obstruction that continues rebirth, one realizes true liberation; by cutting the cognitive obstruction that hinders understanding, one attains great awakening.

terms.root: jñeya「所知」＋ āvaraṇa「障」 · jñeya "the knowable" + āvaraṇa
terms.short_zh: 以法執為根本的障礙，覆蓋所知境、障礙菩提；斷之得大菩提。
terms.short_en: The cognitive obstruction — rooted in grasping at dharmas, it covers the knowable and blocks awakening; ending it brings great awakening.
terms.detail_zh:
所知障由**法執**而生：執著一切法有實在自性，使人不能如實了知一切所知境，障礙菩提（一切智）。它不一定令人輪迴，但使智慧不能圓滿。

**名稱陷阱**：「所知障」不是「知識造成的障礙」，而是「障礙所知（應知之境）的障」。二乘斷煩惱障而未斷所知障，所以證解脫而未成佛。
terms.detail_en:
The cognitive obstruction arises from **grasping at dharmas**: taking all dharmas to have real natures, one cannot know the knowable as it is, which blocks awakening (omniscience). It need not cause rebirth, but it keeps wisdom from completion.

**Naming trap**: 所知障 is not "an obstruction caused by knowledge" but "the obstruction to what is to be known". The two vehicles end the afflictive but not the cognitive obstruction, so they are liberated but not buddhas.

quotes.text: 由我、法執二障具生，若證二空，彼障隨斷。斷障為得二勝果故，由斷續生煩惱障故，證真解脫；由斷礙解所知障故，得大菩提。
quotes.note_en: From grasping at self and at dharmas the two obstructions arise … by cutting the cognitive obstruction that hinders understanding, one attains great awakening.

terms.root: pudgala「補特伽羅、人」＋ nairātmya「無我性」 · pudgala "person" + nairātmya
terms.short_zh: 五蘊和合的有情之中沒有實在的人我；證之斷煩惱障。
terms.short_en: No real personal self in the being made of the aggregates; realizing it ends the afflictive obstruction.
terms.detail_zh:
《大乘百法明門論》結尾：「言無我者，略有二種：一補特伽羅無我、二法無我。」補特伽羅（pudgala）意為「數取趣」——一再往來諸趣的「人」。人無我就是證知這個輪迴的「人」只是五蘊的假合，沒有常一主宰的我。

人無我（我空）對治我執，斷煩惱障，是二乘與大乘共證的。
terms.detail_en:
The Hundred Dharmas treatise concludes: "Non-self is briefly of two kinds: non-self of the person and non-self of dharmas." Pudgala is "the one who again and again takes rebirth" — the person. Selflessness of persons is realizing that this transmigrating "person" is only a composite of aggregates, with no permanent controlling self.

It counters self-grasping and ends the afflictive obstruction; both the two vehicles and the Mahāyāna realize it.

quotes.text: 言無我者，略有二種：一補特伽羅無我、二法無我。
quotes.note_en: As for non-self, it is briefly of two kinds — the non-self of the person and the non-self of dharmas.

terms.root: dharma「法」＋ nairātmya「無我性」 · dharma + nairātmya
terms.short_zh: 構成人的諸法（五蘊等）本身也沒有實在自性；證之斷所知障。大乘的特色見地。
terms.short_en: The dharmas composing a person (aggregates etc.) themselves lack real nature; realizing it ends the cognitive obstruction. A hallmark Mahāyāna insight.
terms.detail_zh:
阿毗達磨把人分析為諸法，破了人我，卻可能執諸法為實有。大乘進一步指出：連五蘊、十二處、十八界等法也是依他而起、如幻不實，沒有獨立自性——這就是法無我（法空）。

法無我對治法執，斷所知障，是成佛所必須。唯識說「二空所顯真如」即圓成實性。
terms.detail_en:
Abhidharma analyses the person into dharmas, undoing the personal self, but may still take the dharmas as real. The Mahāyāna goes further: even the aggregates, bases and elements are dependently arisen, illusion-like, without independent nature — selflessness of dharmas.

It counters grasping at dharmas and ends the cognitive obstruction, required for buddhahood. Yogācāra calls "the suchness disclosed by the two emptinesses" the perfected nature.

quotes.text: 言無我者，略有二種：一補特伽羅無我、二法無我。
quotes.note_en: As for non-self, it is briefly of two kinds — the non-self of the person and the non-self of dharmas.

terms.short_zh: 諸法真實不虛、恆常如此的本性；二空所顯，即圓成實性。
terms.short_en: Suchness — the true, unchanging nature of dharmas, disclosed by the two emptinesses; the perfected nature.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「真謂真實，顯非虛妄；如謂如常，表無變易。」真如是諸法的實性，不是另一個實體，而是法無我、人無我所顯的本性。《大乘五蘊論》：「云何真如？謂諸法法性、法無我性。」

百法中真如列為六無為之一（真如無為），是其他無為法的根本。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "'True' means real, showing it is not false; 'such' means constantly so, indicating that it does not change." Suchness is the real nature of dharmas — not another entity but the nature disclosed by selflessness of persons and dharmas. Pañcaskandhaka: "What is suchness? The dharma-nature of dharmas, their selflessness."

Among the hundred dharmas it is one of the six unconditioned (suchness-unconditioned), the basis of the others.

quotes.text: 真謂真實，顯非虛妄，如謂如常，表無變易
quotes.note_en: "True" means real, showing it is not false; "such" means constantly so, indicating that it does not change.

quotes.text: 云何真如？謂諸法法性、法無我性。
quotes.note_en: What is suchness? The dharma-nature of dharmas, the selflessness of dharmas.

comparisons.title_en: Resolve vs. faith (adhimokṣa & śraddhā)
comparisons.summary_zh: 勝解是認知上的「印持確定」，可正可邪；信是以「心淨」為性的善心所，對實、德、能深忍樂欲。英譯都可能作 conviction，但體性完全不同。
comparisons.summary_en: Resolve is cognitive "sealing" certainty, which may be right or wrong; faith is a wholesome factor whose nature is clarity of mind, accepting and delighting in the real, virtuous and capable. Both get translated "conviction", yet they differ entirely.
comparisons.explanation_zh:
**認知 vs 情意**：勝解是「我確定了」——對已判定的事蓋章認可，他人說不動。它像法官宣判，本身不問對錯：堅信錯誤理論的人也有強烈的勝解。信則以「心淨」為性，含有信忍（接受）、信樂（歡喜）、信欲（嚮往）三面，必定是善的。

**互相配合**：修行中兩者常同時出現——經由聞思而對正法確定（勝解），同時心生澄淨歡喜（信）。但只有勝解而無信，可能流於冷硬的自以為是；只有信而無勝解，則易被動搖。

**相反**：勝解的反面是疑（猶豫不決）；信的反面是不信（心穢、懶惰之依）。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Cognitive vs affective**: resolve is "I am certain" — sealing what has been decided so no one can talk one out of it. Like a judge's verdict, it is not in itself right or wrong: a believer in a false theory can have strong resolve. Faith has clarity of mind as its nature, with acceptance, delight and aspiration, and is always wholesome.

**Working together**: in practice they often arise together — through study and reflection one becomes certain of the Dharma (resolve) while the mind grows clear and glad (faith). Resolve without faith can harden into cold self-righteousness; faith without resolve is easily shaken.

**Opposites**: resolve is opposed by hesitation (doubt); faith by faithlessness (turbidity, the basis of laziness).

quotes.text: 云何勝解？於決定境，印持為性，不可引轉為業。
quotes.note_en: What is resolve? Its nature is confirming and holding to an ascertained object; its function is that it cannot be drawn away.

quotes.text: 云何為信？於實、德、能，深忍、樂、欲，心淨為性；對治不信，樂善為業。
quotes.note_en: What is faith? Its nature is deep acceptance, delight and aspiration toward the real, the virtuous and the capable, with clarity of mind; its function is to counteract faithlessness and delight in the good.

questions.q_zh: 勝解可以是錯誤的（邪勝解）。
questions.q_en: Resolve can be mistaken (wrong resolve).
questions.explain_zh: 勝解只是印持決定境，所印持的可能是邪說。
questions.explain_en: Resolve merely seals what is ascertained, which may be a wrong teaching.

questions.q_zh: 信的體性是？
questions.q_en: What is the nature of faith?
questions.explain_zh: 信「心淨為性」。
questions.explain_en: Faith has "clarity of mind" as its nature.

questions.q_zh: 《成唯識論》所說信的三種對象是？
questions.q_en: What are the three objects of faith in the Cheng weishi lun?

options.en: the real, the virtuous, the capable

questions.explain_zh: 「於實、德、能，深忍、樂、欲。」三寶屬於「德」。
questions.explain_en: "Toward the real, the virtuous and the capable"; the Three Jewels fall under "the virtuous".

questions.q_zh: 勝解的反面主要是？
questions.q_en: Resolve is chiefly opposed by…
questions.explain_zh: 勝解於決定境印持；疑則猶豫不能決定。
questions.explain_en: Resolve seals what is decided; doubt cannot decide.

comparisons.title_en: The four indeterminate factors — regret, sleep, inquiry, investigation
comparisons.summary_zh: 這四者不像遍行那樣遍一切心，不像別境那樣定遍一切地，也不固定為善或染，故名「不定」。其善惡由所伴隨的心決定。
comparisons.summary_en: These four are not in every mind like the omnipresent, not in every realm like the object-specific, and not fixed as wholesome or defiled — hence "indeterminate". Their quality depends on the mind they accompany.
comparisons.explanation_zh:
**為何叫「不定」**：《成唯識論》：「悔、眠、尋、伺於善、染等皆不定故，非如觸等定遍心故，非如欲等定遍地故，立不定名。」三個「不」：不像遍行遍一切心，不像別境遍一切地（界地），善惡也不固定。

**二各二**：《唯識三十頌》說「不定謂悔、眠，尋、伺二各二」。論師對「二各二」有不同解釋，一說悔眠為一組、尋伺為一組，每組又各分染淨二類。

**修行關聯**：悔與掉舉合為「掉悔蓋」，眠與惛沈合為「惛眠蓋」；尋伺的止息則標誌從初禪進入二禪。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Why "indeterminate"**: Cheng weishi lun: "Regret, sleep, inquiry and investigation are not fixed as wholesome, defiled, etc.; unlike contact and the rest they are not in every mind; unlike aspiration and the rest they are not in every realm — hence indeterminate." Three "nots": not universal like the omnipresent, not in all realms like the object-specific, not fixed in moral quality.

**"Two, each two"**: the Thirty Verses say "the indeterminate are regret and sleep, inquiry and investigation — two, each two". Commentators differ; one reading: regret-sleep and inquiry-investigation form two pairs, each further divided into defiled and pure.

**In practice**: regret joins restlessness in the hindrance "restlessness and remorse"; sleep joins torpor in "torpor and sleep"; the stilling of inquiry and investigation marks the passage from the first to the second dhyāna.

quotes.text: 悔、眠、尋、伺於善、染等皆不定故，非如觸等定遍心故，非如欲等定遍地故，立不定名。
quotes.note_en: Regret, sleep, inquiry and investigation are not fixed as wholesome, defiled, etc.; unlike contact and the rest they are not certainly in every mind, and unlike aspiration and the rest they are not certainly in every realm — hence they are called indeterminate.

questions.q_zh: 下列哪一個不是不定心所？
questions.q_en: Which is NOT an indeterminate factor?
questions.explain_zh: 惛沈是大隨煩惱。四不定：悔、眠、尋、伺。
questions.explain_en: Torpor is a major secondary affliction. The four indeterminate are regret, sleep, inquiry, investigation.

questions.q_zh: 後悔自己做了壞事，這種「悔」是善的。
questions.q_en: Regretting a wrong one has done is wholesome regret.
questions.explain_zh: 悔的善惡由所悔之事決定；悔惡是善。
questions.explain_en: Regret takes its quality from what is regretted; regretting evil is wholesome.

questions.q_zh: 惡作（悔）的「業」是？
questions.q_en: What is the function of regret?
questions.explain_zh: 「悔謂惡作……追悔為性，障止為業。」眠則「障觀為業」。
questions.explain_en: Regret "obstructs calm"; sleep "obstructs insight".

questions.q_zh: 「不定」的理由不包括下列哪一項？
questions.q_en: Which is NOT a reason these factors are called indeterminate?

options.en: not fixed as wholesome or defiled

questions.explain_zh: 論中列出的是前三點。
questions.explain_en: The treatise gives the first three reasons.

comparisons.title_zh: 不放逸與精進；放逸與懈怠
comparisons.title_en: Conscientiousness vs. diligence; heedlessness vs. laziness
comparisons.summary_zh: 精進與懈怠是實有的心所；不放逸與放逸則是「組合」出來的：不放逸＝精進＋三善根（防惡修善），放逸＝懈怠＋貪瞋癡（不防不修）。
comparisons.summary_en: Diligence and laziness are real factors; conscientiousness and heedlessness are "composites" — conscientiousness = diligence + the three wholesome roots (guarding and cultivating), heedlessness = laziness + greed, hatred, delusion (neither guarding nor cultivating).

cells.en: Letting go — no guarding or cultivating

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**精進是油門，不放逸是方向盤加煞車**。精進讓人在善法上勇猛向前；但光有衝勁還不夠，還需要「防」（守住不讓惡生起）與「修」（培養善法），而這需要無貪、無瞋、無癡的配合。精進加上三善根共同發揮「防惡修善」的作用，就叫不放逸。

**反面也對稱**：懈怠是實有的懶惰；放逸則是懈怠加上貪瞋癡，使人既不防惡、也不修善，「縱蕩為性」。

**佛陀的遺言**：臨入滅前，佛陀說「無為放逸，我以不放逸故，自致正覺」。不放逸被視為一切善法的總持。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Diligence is the accelerator; conscientiousness is steering plus brakes.** Diligence drives one forward in the good; but drive alone is not enough — one also needs to "guard" (keep evil from arising) and "cultivate" (develop the good), which requires non-greed, non-hatred and non-delusion. Diligence working with the three roots to guard and cultivate is called conscientiousness.

**The opposites mirror this**: laziness is real sluggishness; heedlessness is laziness plus greed, hatred and delusion, so that one neither guards against evil nor cultivates good — "letting go".

**The Buddha's last words**: "Do not be heedless; through heedfulness I attained right awakening." Conscientiousness is regarded as the sum of all good dharmas.

quotes.text: 不放逸者：精進、三根，於所斷、修，防、修為性；對治放逸，成滿一切世、出世間善事為業。
quotes.note_en: Conscientiousness is diligence and the three roots, whose nature is guarding against what is to be abandoned and cultivating what is to be developed; its function is to counteract heedlessness and fulfil all worldly and transcendent good deeds.

quotes.text: 謂由懈怠及貪、瞋、癡，不能防修染淨品法，總名放逸，非別有體。
quotes.note_en: That is, laziness together with greed, hatred and delusion, being unable to guard against and cultivate defiled and pure dharmas, is collectively called heedlessness; it has no separate substance.

questions.q_zh: 不放逸是依哪些法假立的？
questions.q_en: On which dharmas is conscientiousness designated?

options.en: diligence and the three wholesome roots

questions.explain_zh: 「不放逸者：精進、三根……」
questions.explain_en: "Conscientiousness is diligence and the three roots…"

questions.q_zh: 放逸是依哪些法假立的？
questions.q_en: On which dharmas is heedlessness designated?

options.en: it is a separate real factor

questions.explain_zh: 「謂由懈怠及貪、瞋、癡……總名放逸，非別有體。」
questions.explain_en: "Laziness together with greed, hatred and delusion … collectively called heedlessness."

questions.q_zh: 懈怠與精進都是實有的心所。
questions.q_en: Laziness and diligence are both real factors.
questions.explain_zh: 論中判懈怠「定是實有」；精進亦實。
questions.explain_en: The treatise rules laziness definitely real; diligence is real too.

questions.q_zh: 熱衷於做壞事，是否屬於「精進」？
questions.q_en: Is zealous engagement in harmful acts a form of diligence?

options.en: yes, because it is hard work
no — the treatise calls this "also laziness"

questions.explain_zh: 「於諸染事而策勤者，亦名懈怠，退善法故。」
questions.explain_en: "Exerting oneself in defiled affairs is also called laziness, because the good declines."

comparisons.title_zh: 迷與錯：無明（癡）、惡見、疑、不正知與慧
comparisons.title_en: Not knowing and knowing wrongly — ignorance, wrong view, doubt, non-alertness and wisdom
comparisons.summary_zh: 無明是「迷闇」（不明）；惡見是「染慧」（錯誤推度）；疑是「猶豫」（不能決定）；不正知是對當下行為的「謬解」。它們都與「知」有關，但病根不同；慧本身則通善惡。
comparisons.summary_en: Ignorance is darkness (not seeing); wrong view is defiled discernment (reasoning wrongly); doubt is vacillation (not deciding); non-alertness is misreading present conduct. All concern knowing, with different pathologies; prajñā itself can go either way.

cells.zh: 與慧相反；善的對治是無癡

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**四種「不知」的差別**：
- **無明**是根本的「暗」——對事理根本不明白。它是「一切雜染所依」，其他煩惱都在它的基礎上生起。
- **惡見**不是不想，而是想錯了：「顛倒推度，染慧為性」。有身見的人對「我」有一套清楚的推理，只是推錯了。
- **疑**是在真理面前猶豫不決，不肯下判斷。
- **不正知**是在身、語、意的當下行為中覺察錯誤，因而違犯。

**慧的兩面**：慧是別境心所，「簡擇為性，斷疑為業」。如理的慧能斷疑、破無明；而惡見恰恰就是染污的慧。所以佛法說的不是「多思考」就好，而是要「如理」思考。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Four kinds of "not knowing"**:
- **Ignorance** is basic darkness — not understanding at all. It is "the basis of all defilement"; the other afflictions arise on it.
- **Wrong view** is not failing to think but thinking wrongly: "perverse reasoning, defiled discernment". Someone holding self-view has a clear argument for a self — just a wrong one.
- **Doubt** is hesitating before the truth, refusing to judge.
- **Non-alertness** misreads one's present bodily, verbal and mental conduct, and so one transgresses.

**Two faces of prajñā**: prajñā is an object-specific factor, "discrimination by nature, cutting off doubt by function". Sound discernment cuts off doubt and dispels ignorance, yet wrong view is exactly defiled discernment. So the point is not "think more" but "think in accord with reality".

quotes.text: 云何為癡？於諸理、事，迷闇為性；能障無癡，一切雜染所依為業。
quotes.note_en: What is delusion? Its nature is darkness about principles and facts; its function is to obstruct non-delusion and to be the basis of all defilement.

quotes.text: 云何惡見？於諸諦理，顛倒推度，染慧為性；能障善見，招苦為業。
quotes.note_en: What is wrong view? Its nature is defiled discernment that reasons perversely about the truths; its function is to obstruct good view and bring suffering.

questions.q_zh: 哪一個煩惱的體性本身就是「慧」（染慧）？
questions.q_en: Which affliction has (defiled) prajñā as its very nature?
questions.explain_zh: 惡見「顛倒推度，染慧為性」。
questions.explain_en: Wrong view is "perverse reasoning, with defiled discernment as nature".

questions.q_zh: 被稱為「一切雜染所依」的是？
questions.q_en: Which is called "the basis of all defilement"?
questions.explain_zh: 癡「能障無癡，一切雜染所依為業」。
questions.explain_en: Delusion "obstructs non-delusion and is the basis of all defilement".

questions.q_zh: 對四諦猶豫不決，不知是否該相信——這是？
questions.q_en: Wavering about the four truths, not knowing whether to accept them — this is…
questions.explain_zh: 疑「於諸諦理，猶豫為性」。
questions.explain_en: Doubt is "vacillation about the truths".

questions.q_zh: 慧作為心所，必定是善的。
questions.q_en: As a mental factor, prajñā is always wholesome.
questions.explain_zh: 慧屬別境，通善惡；惡見即是染慧。
questions.explain_en: Prajñā is object-specific and variable; wrong view is defiled prajñā.

questions.q_zh: 說話時沒有覺察自己正在口出惡言，事後才發現——這主要是？
questions.q_en: One does not notice while speaking that one's words are harsh, realizing only afterwards. Chiefly…
questions.explain_zh: 不正知「於身語意現前行中不正依住」，導致毀犯。
questions.explain_en: Non-alertness is "not abiding correctly in present conduct of body, speech and mind", leading to transgression.

comparisons.title_en: Seeds, habitual tendencies and latent tendencies
comparisons.summary_zh: 種子側重「能生」（如種生芽），習氣側重「熏成」（如香熏衣），在唯識中是同一潛能的兩個名稱；隨眠則特指煩惱的潛伏狀態。
comparisons.summary_en: "Seed" stresses producing (as a seed yields a sprout), "habitual tendency" stresses being imprinted (as scent perfumes cloth) — two names for the same potential in Yogācāra; "latent tendency" is specifically dormant affliction.

cells.zh: 同種子；亦指斷惑後的餘習
cells.en: Same as seeds; also residue after afflictions end

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**種子與習氣**：《成唯識論》：「何法名為種子？謂本識中親生自果，功能差別。」唯識常以「習氣」為種子的異名，因為種子由現行熏習而成。

**餘習**：「習氣」有時特指煩惱斷後殘留的習慣性傾向——阿羅漢已斷煩惱，仍有餘習；唯佛斷盡。

**隨眠**：《俱舍論》以六隨眠為「諸有本」。唯識把隨眠解為煩惱的種子，現起者名「纏」。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Seeds and tendencies**: Cheng weishi lun: "What is a seed? The potency in the root consciousness that directly produces its own result." Yogācāra often calls seeds "habitual tendencies", since they are formed by the perfuming of activity.

**Residue**: vāsanā sometimes means specifically the residual habits left after afflictions are cut — arhats have ended afflictions but keep residues; only a buddha removes them.

**Latent tendencies**: the Abhidharmakośa calls the six latent tendencies "the root of existence". Yogācāra interprets them as seeds of afflictions; manifest ones are "entanglements".

quotes.text: 何法名為種子？謂本識中親生自果，功能差別。
quotes.note_en: What dharma is called a seed? The particular potency in the root consciousness that directly produces its own result.

questions.q_zh: 「習氣」一詞的比喻來源是？
questions.q_en: The image behind vāsanā is…
questions.explain_zh: vāsanā 原義熏香。
questions.explain_en: Vāsanā originally means perfuming.

questions.q_zh: 在唯識中，種子只指煩惱的潛在狀態。
questions.q_en: In Yogācāra, seeds are only latent afflictions.
questions.explain_zh: 種子通善、惡、無記一切法；只指煩惱潛伏的是隨眠。
questions.explain_en: Seeds cover all dharmas; the term for latent afflictions is anuśaya.

questions.q_zh: 《俱舍論》說隨眠是什麼的根本？
questions.q_en: The Abhidharmakośa calls latent tendencies the root of…
questions.explain_zh: 「隨眠諸有本。」
questions.explain_en: "Latent tendencies are the root of existence."

comparisons.title_en: Aspiration vs. greed (chanda & rāga)
comparisons.summary_zh: 欲是中性的「希望」，可以希求善法（善法欲）；貪是染污的「染著」，是根本煩惱。不可把佛法說的「斷貪」誤解為「斷一切欲」。
comparisons.summary_en: Chanda is neutral wishing and can aim at the good (wholesome aspiration); rāga is defiled attachment, a root affliction. "Abandon greed" does not mean "abandon every wish".

cells.en: Attachment to existence and its means
Can be wholesome, unwholesome or neutral

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**同樣是「想要」，性質不同**。欲只是希望、意向，本身無善惡：想證悟、想幫助眾生是善法欲；想吃午飯是無記的欲；對五欲境的貪求則與貪相應。貪則不同，它的本質是「染著」——黏住不放，必然帶來苦。

**修行不是消滅動力**。《成唯識論》說欲是「勤依」：沒有想要成就的意欲，就不會精進。所以佛法要斷的是貪，而要培養的是對善法的欲。

**中文陷阱**：漢譯「欲」字常兼指兩者（如「欲界」「五欲」「貪欲」）。讀經時要看上下文：作為別境心所的「欲」（chanda）是中性的；「貪欲」（kāma-rāga）則是煩惱。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Both are "wanting", with different natures.** Chanda is just wishing or intending, morally neutral in itself: wishing for awakening or to help beings is wholesome aspiration; wanting lunch is neutral; craving sense objects goes together with greed. Rāga is different: its essence is attachment — sticking fast — which inevitably brings suffering.

**Practice does not kill motivation.** The Cheng weishi lun calls chanda "the support of effort": without aspiration there is no diligence. So Buddhism abandons greed but cultivates aspiration toward the good.

**A Chinese trap**: 欲 is used for both (欲界 "desire realm", 五欲 "five sense pleasures", 貪欲 "sensual greed"). Read the context: the object-specific factor 欲 (chanda) is neutral; 貪欲 (kāma-rāga) is an affliction.

quotes.text: 云何為欲？於所樂境，希望為性，勤依為業。
quotes.note_en: What is aspiration? Its nature is wishing for a desired object; its function is to serve as the support of effort.

quotes.text: 云何為貪？於有、有具，染著為性；能障無貪，生苦為業。
quotes.note_en: What is greed? Its nature is attachment to existence and the means of existence; its function is to obstruct non-greed and produce suffering.

questions.q_zh: 別境心所「欲」本身必定是不善的。
questions.q_en: The object-specific factor chanda is necessarily unwholesome.
questions.explain_zh: 欲通善、惡、無記；希求善法的是善法欲。
questions.explain_en: Chanda may be wholesome, unwholesome or neutral.

questions.q_zh: 依《成唯識論》，欲的「業」（作用）是？
questions.q_en: According to the Cheng weishi lun, what is the function of chanda?
questions.explain_zh: 「希望為性，勤依為業。」
questions.explain_en: "Its nature is wishing; its function is supporting effort."

questions.q_zh: 「想要證悟」屬於？
questions.q_en: "Wishing to attain awakening" is…
questions.explain_zh: 對善法的希求是善法欲，是精進的所依。
questions.explain_en: Wishing for the good is wholesome aspiration, the support of diligence.

questions.q_zh: 在說一切有部，「欲」屬於哪一類？
questions.q_en: In the Sarvāstivāda, chanda belongs to…
questions.explain_zh: 有部列欲為十大地法之一；唯識移入別境。
questions.explain_en: The Sarvāstivāda lists it among the ten universals; Yogācāra moves it to object-specific.

comparisons.title_en: Mind (citta) vs. mental factors (caitasika)
comparisons.summary_zh: 心是主，取總相；心所是伴，兼取別相——如畫師作模、弟子填彩。心所恒依心起、與心相應、繫屬於心。
comparisons.summary_en: Mind is the ruler and grasps the general characteristic; mental factors are its retinue and also grasp particulars — like a master painter outlining and apprentices colouring. Factors always arise dependent on, associated with, and bound to mind.

cells.zh: 受蘊、想蘊，其餘 49 個歸行蘊
cells.en: Feeling, perception; the other 49 in formations

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**心所的三個條件。** 《成唯識論》：「恒依心起，與心相應，繫屬於心，故名心所。」心所不能離心單獨生起；它與心同時、同緣、相應而起；它屬於心，就像「屬我之物」叫做「我所」。

**總相與別相。** 心只把握對象的整體（總相）；心所除了總體之外，還把握種種特殊面向（別相）——受把握其可意與否，想把握其相狀，思把握其正因與否。所以說心所「助成心事」。

**相應的五義。** 《俱舍論》頌說心與心所「相應義有五」：所依、所緣、行相、時、事五者平等——同依一根、同緣一境、行相相似、同時生起、各一體而相伴。

**心、意、識。** 在說一切有部，心、意、識是同一體的三個名稱；在唯識，三名雖通八識，但第八名心、第七名意、前六名識。無論哪一說，它們都屬「心」一邊，而不是心所。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Three conditions for a mental factor.** Cheng weishi lun: "They always arise dependent on mind, are associated with mind, and are bound to mind — hence 'what mind possesses'." A factor cannot arise apart from mind; it arises simultaneously, with the same object, in association with it; and it belongs to mind as "mine" belongs to "me".
