**General vs. particular characteristics.** Mind grasps the object as a whole; mental factors grasp particular aspects as well — feeling its agreeableness, perception its features, volition whether it is a right cause — so they "help accomplish the work of mind".

**Five senses of "association".** The Abhidharmakośa verse says mind and factors are "associated in five respects": same basis (faculty), same object, similar mode of apprehension, same time, and each one a single entity.

**Citta, manas, vijñāna.** For the Sarvāstivāda these are three names of one entity; for Yogācāra the three names apply to all eight consciousnesses but most aptly the eighth is citta, the seventh manas, the first six vijñāna. Either way they are all on the "mind" side, not mental factors.

quotes.text: 恒依心起，與心相應，繫屬於心，故名心所，如屬我物，立我所名。心於所緣，唯取總相；心所於彼，亦取別相，助成心事，得心所名。如畫師、資，作模、填彩。
quotes.note_en: Because they always arise dependent on mind, are associated with mind and bound to mind, they are called mental factors, as things belonging to me are called "mine". Mind grasps only the general characteristic of its object; mental factors grasp particular characteristics too, helping accomplish mind's work — like a master painter and apprentices, one outlining, the others colouring.

quotes.text: 心意識體一，心心所有依，有緣有行相，相應義有五。
quotes.note_en: Citta, manas and vijñāna are one in essence. Mind and mental factors have a basis, have an object, have a mode of apprehension, and are associated — "association" has five senses.

questions.q_zh: 依《成唯識論》的畫師喻，心所的作用相當於？
questions.q_en: In the Cheng weishi lun's painter simile, what do mental factors do?
questions.explain_zh: 「如畫師、資，作模、填彩」——心如畫師作模，心所如弟子填彩。
questions.explain_en: Mind is the master drawing the outline; mental factors are apprentices filling in colour.

questions.q_zh: 心與心所各取對象的什麼？
questions.q_en: What do mind and mental factors each grasp of the object?

options.zh: 心唯取總相，心所亦取別相
options.en: Mind only the general characteristic; factors particular ones too
Mind the particular, factors the general

questions.explain_zh: 「心於所緣，唯取總相；心所於彼，亦取別相。」
questions.explain_en: "Mind grasps only the general characteristic; mental factors also grasp particular characteristics."

questions.q_zh: 在百法中，八識屬於「心法」，不屬於心所。
questions.q_en: In the hundred dharmas, the eight consciousnesses are "mind" dharmas, not mental factors.
questions.explain_zh: 百法第一「心法」八種即八識；心所有法五十一種另列。
questions.explain_en: The first category, "mind", consists of the eight consciousnesses; the 51 factors are a separate category.

questions.q_zh: 下列何者**不是**《成唯識論》所說心所的條件？
questions.q_en: Which is NOT one of the Cheng weishi lun's conditions for a mental factor?
questions.explain_zh: 心所必依心而起，不能獨自生起。
questions.explain_en: Mental factors always depend on mind and cannot arise alone.

questions.q_zh: 《俱舍論》如何看心、意、識？
questions.q_en: How does the Abhidharmakośa view citta, manas and vijñāna?
questions.explain_zh: 「心意識體一」；「集起故名心，思量故名意，了別故名識」。
questions.explain_en: "Citta, manas, vijñāna are one in essence" — named by accumulating, deliberating, discerning.

questions.q_zh: 依《成唯識論》「隨勝顯」之說，哪一識最名為「意」？
questions.q_en: By the Cheng weishi lun's "named by prominence", which consciousness is most aptly called manas?
questions.explain_zh: 「第七名意，緣藏識等，恒、審思量，為我等故。」注意：第六「意識」的「意」是指其所依根，並非「最名為意」。
questions.explain_en: "The seventh is called manas: taking the store-consciousness as object, it constantly and intently deliberates, [taking it] as self." Note: the "mano-" of the sixth consciousness refers to its basis, not to this naming.

comparisons.title_en: The four fruits of the disciple path
comparisons.summary_zh: 須陀洹（斷三結）→ 斯陀含（貪瞋癡薄）→ 阿那含（斷五下分結，不還欲界）→ 阿羅漢（斷盡一切煩惱，不受後有）。
comparisons.summary_en: Stream-enterer (three fetters cut) → once-returner (greed, hatred, delusion weakened) → non-returner (five lower fetters cut, not returning to the desire realm) → arhat (all afflictions ended, no further birth).
comparisons.explanation_zh:
《雜阿含經》：「三結斷得須陀洹……七有天人往生，究竟苦邊。」「三結盡，貪、恚、癡薄，得斯陀含。」「五下分結盡，生般涅槃阿那含。」阿羅漢則自說：「我生已盡，梵行已立，所作已作，自知不受後有。」

五下分結＝三結＋欲貪＋瞋恚；阿羅漢再斷五上分結（色貪、無色貪、掉舉、慢、無明）。
comparisons.explanation_en:
Saṃyuktāgama: "Cutting the three fetters one becomes a stream-enterer … reborn at most seven times, reaching the end of suffering." "The three fetters ended, greed, hatred and delusion weakened — once-returner." "The five lower fetters ended — non-returner." The arhat declares: "Birth is ended, the holy life lived, what had to be done is done; there is no further existence."

The five lower fetters = the three plus sensual desire and ill will; the arhat also cuts the five higher (desire for form and formless existence, restlessness, pride, ignorance).

quotes.text: 三結斷得須陀洹，不墮惡趣法，決定正趣三菩提，七有天人往生，究竟苦邊
quotes.note_en: Having cut the three fetters one attains stream-entry, is not subject to the lower destinies, is certain of awakening, is reborn at most seven times among gods and humans, and reaches the end of suffering.

questions.q_zh: 斷五下分結而得的是？
questions.q_en: Cutting the five lower fetters yields…
questions.explain_zh: 「五下分結盡，生般涅槃阿那含。」
questions.explain_en: "The five lower fetters ended — non-returner."

questions.q_zh: 三結不包括下列哪一項？
questions.q_en: Which is NOT one of the three fetters?
questions.explain_zh: 瞋恚屬五下分結中的後二結之一。
questions.explain_en: Ill will is among the two extra lower fetters.

questions.q_zh: 須陀洹最多再往返人天七次。
questions.q_en: A stream-enterer is reborn at most seven more times.
questions.explain_zh: 「七有天人往生，究竟苦邊。」
questions.explain_en: "Reborn at most seven times … reaching the end of suffering."

comparisons.title_en: Self-respect vs. decorum (hrī & apatrāpya)
comparisons.summary_zh: 兩者都是對過惡的羞恥，差別在羞恥的依據：慚依「自」與「法」（向內），愧依「世間」（向外）。反面是無慚、無愧。
comparisons.summary_en: Both are shame at wrongdoing; they differ in what the shame relies on — hrī on oneself and the Dharma (inward), apatrāpya on the world (outward). Their opposites are the two intermediate secondary afflictions.

cells.zh: 自力、法力（自增上、法增上）

cells.en: Counters lack of self-respect; stops misconduct
Counters lack of decorum; stops misconduct

cells.zh: 向內：對不起自己與正法
cells.en: Inward: letting down oneself and the Dharma

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**共同點**：慚與愧的作用完全相同——「止息惡行為業」，而且都對「所作罪」生羞恥。

**差別在「依」**：《成唯識論》說慚「依自、法力」，愧「依世間力」。一個人不做壞事，可能是因為「這不是我這樣的人該做的、違背我所學的法」（慚），也可能是因為「別人會怎麼看我」（愧）。前者向內，後者向外。

**為何要兩個**：只靠內在的自尊，可能自以為是；只靠外在的眼光，沒人看見時就放縱。佛陀稱二者為「護世間」的「二淨法」，缺一不可。

**反面**：無慚「不顧自、法」，無愧「不顧世間」；二者遍於一切不善心，是中隨煩惱，《成唯識論》判為實有。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**In common**: their function is identical — "stopping misconduct" — and both feel shame at wrong done.

**The difference is the basis**: the Cheng weishi lun says hrī "relies on the power of oneself and the Dharma", apatrāpya "on the power of the world". One may refrain from wrong because "this is unworthy of who I am and contrary to the Dharma I follow" (hrī), or because "what would others think?" (apatrāpya). Inward versus outward.

**Why both**: self-respect alone can become self-righteous; concern for others' opinion alone lapses when no one is watching. The Buddha calls them "two pure dharmas that protect the world" — both are needed.

**Opposites**: lack of self-respect "disregards oneself and the Dharma", lack of decorum "disregards the world"; both accompany every unwholesome mind (intermediate secondary afflictions) and are ruled to be real.

quotes.text: 有二淨法，能護世間。何等為二？所謂慚、愧。
quotes.note_en: There are two pure dharmas that protect the world. What are the two? Namely, self-respect and decorum.

questions.q_zh: 依《成唯識論》，「愧」所依的是什麼力量？
questions.q_en: According to the Cheng weishi lun, what does apatrāpya rely on?
questions.explain_zh: 慚「依自、法力」，愧「依世間力」。
questions.explain_en: Hrī relies on oneself and the Dharma; apatrāpya on the world.

questions.q_zh: 慚與愧的「業」（作用）相同，都是止息惡行。
questions.q_en: Hrī and apatrāpya have the same function — stopping misconduct.
questions.explain_zh: 兩者都是「止息惡行為業」，差別只在所依與體性。
questions.explain_en: Both have "stopping misconduct" as function; they differ in basis and nature.

questions.q_zh: 某人獨處無人看見時也不肯做虧心事，主要是哪一心所的作用？
questions.q_en: Someone refuses to do wrong even when completely alone and unseen. Which factor is chiefly at work?
questions.explain_zh: 無人看見時仍不作惡，是依自身與正法而羞恥——慚。
questions.explain_en: Refraining when unseen relies on oneself and the Dharma — self-respect.

questions.q_zh: 無慚、無愧屬於哪一類隨煩惱？
questions.q_en: Which class of secondary afflictions do lack of self-respect and lack of decorum belong to?
questions.explain_zh: 「無慚等二，遍不善故，名中隨煩惱。」
questions.explain_en: "The two beginning with lack of self-respect pervade all unwholesome minds, hence intermediate."

questions.q_zh: 佛陀稱慚與愧為「能護世間」的二淨法。
questions.q_en: The Buddha called hrī and apatrāpya the two pure dharmas that protect the world.
questions.explain_zh: 《雜阿含經》：「有二淨法，能護世間……所謂慚、愧。」
questions.explain_en: Saṃyuktāgama: "There are two pure dharmas that protect the world … self-respect and decorum."

comparisons.title_en: Afflictions vs. latent tendencies
comparisons.summary_zh: 煩惱泛指擾亂身心的心所；隨眠是潛伏的煩惱。有部以隨眠即煩惱；經部與唯識以隨眠為煩惱的種子，現起者稱纏。
comparisons.summary_en: Afflictions are the disturbing mental factors in general; latent tendencies are dormant afflictions. The Sarvāstivāda equates them; the Sautrāntika and Yogācāra take latent tendencies as seeds of afflictions, the manifest ones being "entanglements".

cells.en: greed, aversion, delusion, pride, doubt, wrong view
greed, aversion, pride, ignorance, views, doubt

comparisons.explanation_zh:
兩者列出的六種內容相同，只是名稱與次序略異。《唯識三十頌》：「煩惱謂貪、瞋、癡、慢、疑、惡見。」《俱舍論》：「隨眠諸有本，此差別有六。」

隨眠的觀念解釋了為什麼一個人此刻心平氣和，遇境卻又生起煩惱——煩惱並沒有斷，只是潛伏著。
comparisons.explanation_en:
The two lists of six are the same, differing only in names and order. Thirty Verses: "The afflictions are greed, aversion, delusion, pride, doubt and wrong view." Abhidharmakośa: "The latent tendencies are the root of existence; they are six."

The idea explains why someone calm now flares up when conditions arise: the affliction was not cut, only dormant.

quotes.text: 隨眠諸有本，此差別有六，謂貪瞋亦慢，無明見及疑。
quotes.note_en: The latent tendencies are the root of existence; they are of six kinds — greed, aversion, pride, ignorance, views and doubt.

questions.q_zh: 唯識如何解釋隨眠？
questions.q_en: How does Yogācāra interpret latent tendencies?
questions.explain_zh: 經部與唯識以隨眠為煩惱種子。
questions.explain_en: Sautrāntika and Yogācāra take them as seeds of afflictions.

questions.q_zh: 六隨眠與六根本煩惱內容相同。
questions.q_en: The six latent tendencies have the same content as the six root afflictions.
questions.explain_zh: 無明即癡，見即惡見，名稱與次序不同而已。
questions.explain_en: Ignorance = delusion, views = wrong view; only names and order differ.

comparisons.title_en: The eleven wholesome factors and what each counteracts
comparisons.summary_zh: 每一個善心所都「對治」一個煩惱：信↔不信、精進↔懈怠、慚↔無慚、愧↔無愧、無貪↔貪、無瞋↔瞋、無癡↔癡、輕安↔惛沈、不放逸↔放逸、行捨↔掉舉、不害↔害。
comparisons.summary_en: Each wholesome factor counteracts an affliction: faith ↔ faithlessness, diligence ↔ laziness, self-respect ↔ its lack, decorum ↔ its lack, non-greed ↔ greed, non-hatred ↔ aversion, non-delusion ↔ delusion, pliancy ↔ torpor, conscientiousness ↔ heedlessness, equanimity ↔ restlessness, non-harming ↔ harmfulness.
comparisons.explanation_zh:
**一一相對**：《成唯識論》在每個善心所的定義中都明說「對治」什麼：信「對治不信」、精進「對治懈怠」、輕安「對治惛沈」、行捨「對治掉舉」……這使十一善心所成為一套完整的「解藥清單」。

**三個假立的**：不放逸與行捨都是「精進、三根」在不同作用上的假立——防惡修善叫不放逸，令心平等正直叫行捨；不害是「無瞋」在不損惱有情上的假立。其餘八個是實有。

**對照放逸**：放逸也是假立的——「由懈怠及貪、瞋、癡……總名放逸」，與不放逸的「精進＋三善根」恰好一一相反。

**怎麼用**：修行時發現自己惛沈，就修輕安（調身調息、令身心輕快）；發現掉舉，就修行捨（放下、平等）；發現懈怠，就修精進——並以信作為一切的起點。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Point by point**: in defining each wholesome factor the Cheng weishi lun says what it counteracts: faith "counteracts faithlessness", diligence "laziness", pliancy "torpor", equanimity "restlessness"… The eleven thus form a complete "list of antidotes".

**Three designated ones**: conscientiousness and equanimity are both "diligence and the three roots" named by different functions — guarding against evil and cultivating good is conscientiousness, making the mind even and upright is equanimity; non-harming is non-hatred named for not injuring beings. The other eight are real.

**Mirror image**: heedlessness is also designated — "laziness together with greed, hatred and delusion … collectively called heedlessness" — the exact inverse of conscientiousness's "diligence plus the three wholesome roots".

**Using it**: noticing torpor, cultivate pliancy (settling body and breath, lightening body and mind); noticing restlessness, cultivate equanimity (letting go, evenness); noticing laziness, cultivate diligence — with faith as the starting point of everything.

questions.q_zh: 輕安對治的是？
questions.q_en: Pliancy counteracts…
questions.explain_zh: 輕安「對治惛沈，轉依為業」。
questions.explain_en: Pliancy "counteracts torpor".

questions.q_zh: 行捨對治的是？
questions.q_en: Equanimity counteracts…
questions.explain_zh: 行捨「對治掉舉，靜住為業」。
questions.explain_en: Equanimity "counteracts restlessness".

questions.q_zh: 下列哪一個善心所是依「無瞋」假立的？
questions.q_en: Which wholesome factor is designated on non-hatred?
questions.explain_zh: 論中說不害是「即無瞋」，於有情不為損惱而假立。
questions.explain_en: Non-harming is non-hatred, designated for not injuring beings.

questions.q_zh: 不放逸與行捨都是依精進與三善根假立的。
questions.q_en: Conscientiousness and equanimity are both designated on diligence and the three wholesome roots.
questions.explain_zh: 兩者定義都以「精進、三根」開頭。
questions.explain_en: Both definitions begin with "diligence and the three roots".

questions.q_zh: 精進對治的是？
questions.q_en: Diligence counteracts…
questions.explain_zh: 精進「對治懈怠，滿善為業」。
questions.explain_en: Diligence "counteracts laziness, fulfilling the good".

questions.q_zh: 十一善心所中有幾個是假立的？
questions.q_en: How many of the eleven wholesome factors are designated rather than real?
questions.explain_zh: 不放逸、行捨、不害三者假立，其餘八者實有。
questions.explain_en: Conscientiousness, equanimity and non-harming; the other eight are real.

comparisons.title_en: Loving-kindness vs. compassion; non-hatred vs. non-harming
comparisons.summary_zh: 慈是與樂、悲是拔苦。在心所上，慈的基礎是無瞋，悲的基礎是不害；所對治的分別是瞋與害。
comparisons.summary_en: Loving-kindness gives happiness, compassion removes suffering. As mental factors, kindness rests on non-hatred and compassion on non-harming; they counter aversion and harmfulness respectively.
comparisons.explanation_zh:
《成唯識論》：「無瞋與樂，不害拔苦。」《大乘五蘊論》說無瞋「以慈為性」，不害「以悲為性」。《大智度論》說「慈名愛念眾生，常求安隱樂事以饒益之；悲名愍念眾生受五道中種種身苦、心苦」。

兩者常並稱「慈悲」，但方向不同：慈看眾生的快樂而願其增長，悲看眾生的痛苦而願其止息。
comparisons.explanation_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Non-hatred gives happiness, non-harming removes suffering." The Pañcaskandhaka says non-hatred "has loving-kindness as its nature", non-harming "compassion". The Dazhidu lun: loving-kindness is "cherishing beings, seeking their peace and happiness"; compassion is "pitying beings who suffer in body and mind".

They are usually paired, but face different ways: kindness looks at beings' happiness and wishes it to grow; compassion looks at their suffering and wishes it to end.

quotes.text: 無瞋，翻對斷物命瞋；不害，正違損惱物害。無瞋與樂；不害拔苦。
quotes.note_en: Non-hatred opposes the hatred that takes life; non-harming opposes the harmfulness that torments beings. Non-hatred gives happiness; non-harming removes suffering.

questions.q_zh: 「拔苦」是哪一個？
questions.q_en: Which one "removes suffering"?
questions.explain_zh: 慈與樂，悲拔苦。
questions.explain_en: Kindness gives happiness, compassion removes suffering.

questions.q_zh: 悲的心所基礎是？
questions.q_en: What is the mental-factor basis of compassion?
questions.explain_zh: 不害「悲愍為業」。
questions.explain_en: Non-harming "has compassion as its function".

questions.q_zh: 《大乘五蘊論》說無瞋「以慈為性」。
questions.q_en: The Pañcaskandhaka says non-hatred "has loving-kindness as its nature".
questions.explain_zh: 「云何無瞋？謂瞋對治，以慈為性。」
questions.explain_en: "What is non-hatred? The antidote to hatred; its nature is loving-kindness."

comparisons.title_en: Pride vs. haughtiness (māna & mada)
comparisons.summary_zh: 慢是「和別人比」而高舉（根本煩惱，以比較為核心）；憍是對自己的盛事陶醉（隨煩惱，貪的一分），不必比較。
comparisons.summary_en: Pride exalts oneself by comparison with others (a root affliction); haughtiness is intoxication with one's own fortune (a secondary affliction, part of greed), needing no comparison.

cells.en: Relying on self over others — comparison
Attached to one's own flourishing — intoxication

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**比較 vs 陶醉**：慢的定義是「恃己於他，高舉為性」——一定有一個「他」作比較：我比你強、我和你一樣（其實不如）、我雖不如你但也差不多……所以有七慢之分。憍則是「於自盛事，深生染著，醉傲為性」：對自己的年輕、健康、財富、才華感到陶醉，不需要與誰比較。

**根本與分支**：慢是六根本煩惱之一；憍是小隨煩惱，「貪愛一分為體」——本質上是對自身所有的貪著。

**最深的慢**：我慢（asmimāna），即執五取蘊為我而心高舉，與第七末那識恆時相應，直到修道斷盡。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Comparison vs intoxication**: pride is "relying on oneself, holding oneself high over others" — there is always an "other": I am better than you, I am your equal (though not), I am a bit less but still… — hence the seven kinds. Haughtiness is "deep attachment to one's own flourishing, intoxicated pride": delight in one's youth, health, wealth or talent, with no comparison needed.

**Root and branch**: pride is one of the six root afflictions; haughtiness is a minor secondary affliction with "a part of greed" as substance — at bottom, attachment to what one has.

**The deepest pride**: the pride of "I am" (asmimāna), taking the aggregates as self; it constantly accompanies the seventh consciousness, manas, until uprooted on the path.

quotes.text: 云何為慢？恃己於他，高舉為性；能障不慢，生苦為業。
quotes.note_en: What is pride? Relying on oneself, its nature is holding oneself high over others; its function is to obstruct humility and produce suffering.

quotes.text: 云何為憍？於自盛事，深生染著，醉傲為性；能障不憍，染依為業。
quotes.note_en: What is haughtiness? Its nature is deep attachment to one's own flourishing, intoxicated pride; its function is to obstruct non-haughtiness and be the basis of defilement.

questions.q_zh: 一個人獨處時，對著鏡子欣賞自己的年輕美貌而陶醉——這主要是？
questions.q_en: Alone in front of a mirror, someone is intoxicated with their own youth and looks. This is chiefly…
questions.explain_zh: 憍是「於自盛事，深生染著，醉傲」，不必與他人比較。
questions.explain_en: Haughtiness is intoxication with one's own flourishing, with no comparison needed.

questions.q_zh: 「我的修行比他高多了」——這是？
questions.q_en: "My practice is far above his." This is…
questions.explain_zh: 與他人比較而高舉，是慢。
questions.explain_en: Exalting oneself by comparison is pride.

questions.q_zh: 憍的體性是貪愛的一分。
questions.q_en: Haughtiness has a part of greed as its substance.
questions.explain_zh: 「此亦貪愛一分為體，離貪無別憍相用故。」
questions.explain_en: "This too has a part of greed as substance."

questions.q_zh: 未證得聖果卻自以為已證得，屬七慢中的哪一種？
questions.q_en: Thinking one has attained a realization one has not reached is which of the seven kinds of pride?
questions.explain_zh: 增上慢：「於未得增上殊勝所證法中謂我已得。」
questions.explain_en: Conceit of attainment: "claiming to have attained a superior realization not yet reached."

questions.q_zh: 哪一種慢與第七末那識恆時相應？
questions.q_en: Which kind of pride constantly accompanies the seventh consciousness, manas?
questions.explain_zh: 末那識恆與我癡、我見、我慢、我愛四煩惱相應。
questions.explain_en: Manas is always accompanied by self-delusion, self-view, self-pride and self-love.

comparisons.title_en: Manas, mental consciousness and the seventh consciousness
comparisons.summary_zh: 「意」是意根（第六識的所依）；「意識」是依意根而起的第六識；「末那識」是恆緣阿賴耶識執以為我的第七識——唯識以末那為意根。
comparisons.summary_en: Manas is the mental faculty (support of the sixth consciousness); mano-vijñāna is the sixth consciousness based on it; kliṣṭa-manas is the seventh, which constantly grasps the ālaya as self — Yogācāra identifies it as the mental faculty.

cells.zh: 第六識，五位無心時中斷
cells.en: Sixth; interrupted in five mindless states
Constant deliberation; four afflictions always present

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**三個名字**：梵語 manas 意為「意」；mano-vijñāna 是「依意之識」；「末那」是 manas 的音譯，加上「染污」（kliṣṭa）以表第七識。

**有部**：《俱舍論》：「由即六識身，無間滅為意」——意根只是剛滅的前念之識，沒有第七識。

**唯識**：意識需要一個恆常的同時所依，所以立第七末那識為意根。末那識「依彼轉緣彼，思量為性相」，恆時執阿賴耶識為我，與我癡、我見、我慢、我愛四煩惱相應。

**意識 vs 末那**：意識的我執時有時無（睡眠、悶絕時中斷）；末那的我執恆常不斷，是俱生我執的根本。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Three names**: manas means "mind"; mano-vijñāna is "consciousness based on manas"; 末那 transliterates manas, qualified as "afflicted" (kliṣṭa) for the seventh consciousness.

**Sarvāstivāda**: Abhidharmakośa: "Any of the six consciousnesses, having just ceased, is manas" — the mental faculty is just the preceding moment of consciousness; there is no seventh.

**Yogācāra**: the mental consciousness needs a constant simultaneous support, so the seventh consciousness is posited as the mental faculty. It "depends on that and takes that as object; deliberation is its nature", constantly grasping the ālaya as self, with self-delusion, self-view, self-pride and self-love.

**Mental consciousness vs manas**: the former's self-grasping comes and goes (interrupted in sleep or fainting); that of manas never stops — the root of innate self-grasping.

quotes.text: 由即六識身，無間滅為意。
quotes.note_en: Any of the six bodies of consciousness, having just ceased, is manas.

quotes.text: 次第二能變，是識名末那，依彼轉緣彼，思量為性相。
quotes.note_en: Next is the second transformation: this consciousness is called manas; it depends on that and takes that as object; deliberation is its nature and characteristic.

questions.q_zh: 末那識的所緣是？
questions.q_en: What does the seventh consciousness take as object?
questions.explain_zh: 「依彼轉緣彼」——依阿賴耶、緣阿賴耶，執以為我。
questions.explain_en: "It depends on that and takes that as object" — the ālaya, grasped as self.

questions.q_zh: 在說一切有部，意根是什麼？
questions.q_en: In the Sarvāstivāda, what is the mental faculty?

options.en: the consciousness that has just ceased

questions.explain_zh: 「由即六識身，無間滅為意。」
questions.explain_en: "Any of the six consciousnesses, having just ceased, is manas."

questions.q_zh: 第六意識在深度睡眠、悶絕時會中斷，末那識則不中斷。
questions.q_en: The sixth consciousness is interrupted in deep sleep and fainting; manas is not.
questions.explain_zh: 意識有五位無心；末那恆審思量，唯阿羅漢、滅定、出世道不起。
questions.explain_en: The sixth has five mindless states; manas continues, absent only in arhats, cessation and the transcendent path.

questions.q_zh: 「末那」二字是什麼？
questions.q_en: What is 末那?
questions.explain_zh: 末那即 manas 的音譯。
questions.explain_en: 末那 transliterates manas.

comparisons.title_en: Concealment, deceit, guile — three kinds of deception
comparisons.summary_zh: 覆是藏起自己「有」的過失；誑是假裝自己「有」其實沒有的德行；諂是為了籠絡他人而扭曲自己、曲意逢迎。三者皆以貪、癡為體。
comparisons.summary_en: Concealment hides faults one has; deceit feigns virtues one lacks; guile twists oneself to ensnare others. All three are parts of greed and delusion.

cells.en: Puts on manners to net others
Fear of losing gain and fame
Part of greed and delusion (one view: delusion)

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**一藏、一裝、一曲**：覆是「減法」——把自己有的過失藏起來；誑是「加法」——把自己沒有的德行裝出來；諂則是「變形」——為了討好、籠絡他人而扭曲自己的言行，心術險曲。

**動機都與名利有關**：覆「恐失利、譽」，誑「為獲利譽」，所以都含有貪的成分；又不明白這樣做只會增長過患，所以含有癡的成分。三者都是小隨煩惱，「定是假有」。

**後果**：覆的人日後內心悔惱；誑的人走上邪命；諂的人則聽不進師友的正直教誨，因為他總在揣摩對方、掩飾自己。修行的對治是「發露懺悔」與質直心。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Hide, fake, twist**: concealment "subtracts" — hiding faults one has; deceit "adds" — displaying virtues one lacks; guile "distorts" — bending one's words and manners to please or ensnare others.

**All motivated by gain and fame**: concealment fears losing them, deceit seeks them — hence greed; not seeing that this only multiplies harm — hence delusion. All three are minor secondary afflictions, "definitely designated".

**Consequences**: the concealer is later gnawed by remorse; the deceiver slides into wrong livelihood; the guileful cannot take in the straightforward counsel of teachers and friends, being always calculating and covering. The remedy is open confession and a straightforward mind.

quotes.text: 云何為誑？為獲利譽，矯現有德，詭詐為性；能障不誑，邪命為業。
quotes.note_en: What is deceit? For the sake of profit and fame, its nature is feigning virtue with trickery; its function is to obstruct non-deceit and lead to wrong livelihood.

quotes.text: 此亦貪、癡一分為體，離二無別諂相用故。
quotes.note_en: This too has a part of greed and delusion as substance; apart from these two there is no characteristic or function of guile.

questions.q_zh: 犯了錯卻不讓人知道，怕名聲受損——這是？
questions.q_en: One has done wrong but keeps it hidden for fear of one's reputation. This is…
questions.explain_zh: 覆：「於自作罪，恐失利、譽，隱藏為性。」
questions.explain_en: Concealment: "hiding one's own wrongdoing for fear of losing gain and reputation."

questions.q_zh: 明明沒有修行功夫，卻裝出很有德行的樣子以獲得供養——這是？
questions.q_en: With no real practice, one poses as virtuous to receive offerings. This is…
questions.explain_zh: 誑：「為獲利譽，矯現有德，詭詐為性；……邪命為業。」
questions.explain_en: Deceit: "to obtain profit and fame, feigning virtue … wrong livelihood."

questions.q_zh: 為了討好上司而刻意逢迎、說違心話——這是？
questions.q_en: To please the boss one fawns and says things one does not mean. This is…
questions.explain_zh: 諂：「為網他故，矯設異儀，險、曲為性。」
questions.explain_en: Guile: "to net others, contriving unusual manners; crooked."

questions.q_zh: 誑與諂都以貪、癡的一分為體。
questions.q_en: Deceit and guile both have parts of greed and delusion as their substance.
questions.explain_zh: 論中說誑、諂皆「貪、癡一分為體，離二無別……相用」。
questions.explain_en: Both are "parts of greed and delusion".

questions.q_zh: 哪一個的「業」是「邪命」？
questions.q_en: Which one has "wrong livelihood" as its function?
questions.explain_zh: 誑以詐現有德謀取利養，所以「邪命為業」。
questions.explain_en: Deceit wins offerings by feigned virtue, hence wrong livelihood.

comparisons.title_zh: 種種「滅」：擇滅、非擇滅、滅盡定、涅槃
comparisons.title_en: Kinds of cessation — through discernment, not through discernment, the attainment, nirvāṇa
comparisons.summary_zh: 擇滅＝由慧斷惑所證之滅＝涅槃（無為）；非擇滅是缺緣不生（無為，非解脫）；滅盡定是暫時止息心識的定（有為的不相應行）。
comparisons.summary_en: Cessation through discernment = cessation won by wisdom = nirvāṇa (unconditioned); cessation not through discernment is non-arising for lack of conditions (unconditioned, not liberation); the attainment of cessation is a temporary stilling of mind (a conditioned non-associated formation).
comparisons.explanation_zh:
《大乘五蘊論》：「云何擇滅？謂若滅是離繫……由煩惱對治故諸蘊畢竟不生。」「云何非擇滅？謂若滅非離繫……離煩惱對治而諸蘊畢竟不生。」

判別關鍵有二：是否由**慧**（擇）而得；是否**離繫**（脫離煩惱）。只有擇滅兩者皆是，所以擇滅即涅槃。滅盡定雖名為「滅」，卻是有時限的定，出定後心識再起。
comparisons.explanation_en:
Pañcaskandhaka: "What is cessation through discernment? A cessation that is disjunction … through the antidote to afflictions the aggregates never arise again." "What is cessation not through discernment? A cessation that is not disjunction … the aggregates never arise, apart from any antidote."

Two tests: is it won by **wisdom** (discernment)? is it **disjunction** (release from afflictions)? Only the first cessation passes both, so it is nirvāṇa. The attainment of cessation, despite its name, is a time-limited meditative state; mind returns on emerging.

quotes.text: 云何擇滅？謂若滅是離繫。此復云何？謂由煩惱對治故諸蘊畢竟不生。
quotes.note_en: What is cessation through discernment? A cessation that is disjunction. What is it? Because of the antidote to the afflictions, the aggregates never arise again.

questions.q_zh: 哪一種滅即是涅槃？
questions.q_en: Which cessation is nirvāṇa?
questions.explain_zh: 擇滅由慧斷惑、是離繫，即涅槃。
questions.explain_en: It is won by wisdom and is disjunction — nirvāṇa.

questions.q_zh: 滅盡定屬於無為法。
questions.q_en: The attainment of cessation is unconditioned.
questions.explain_zh: 滅盡定是心不相應行，屬有為；「想受滅無為」則是依之假立的無為。
questions.explain_en: It is a non-associated formation (conditioned); "cessation of perception and feeling" as an unconditioned is designated on it.

questions.q_zh: 專心看畫時沒聽到的聲音，那一刻的耳識永不生起——這屬於？
questions.q_en: Absorbed in a painting, a sound goes unheard and that ear-consciousness never arises. This is…
questions.explain_zh: 缺緣不生，非由慧力，是非擇滅。
questions.explain_en: Non-arising for lack of conditions, not through wisdom.

comparisons.title_zh: 瞋的五種分位：忿、恨、惱、嫉、害
comparisons.title_en: Five faces of aversion — wrath, resentment, spite, jealousy, harmfulness
comparisons.summary_zh: 忿、恨、惱、嫉、害都「以瞋恚一分為體」，沒有獨立實體，是瞋在不同情境下的表現：當下爆發、事後積怨、惡言螫人、見人好而妒、無悲而損惱。
comparisons.summary_en: Wrath, resentment, spite, jealousy and harmfulness all "have a part of aversion as substance" — no separate entity, just aversion in different situations — erupting now, festering later, stinging with words, begrudging others' success, tormenting without compassion.
comparisons.explanation_zh:
**同一根源**：《成唯識論》對五者都說「此即（亦）瞋恚一分為體，離瞋無別忿（恨……）相用故」。它們是小隨煩惱，各別生起，「定是假有」——只是給瞋在特定情境下的面貌取了名字。

**時間序列：忿 → 恨 → 惱**。當下怒氣爆發是忿；忿過之後怨氣不散是恨；恨積在心，追憶往事、觸動舊怨，於是惡言相向是惱。

**對象不同：嫉與害**。嫉是見他人榮盛而不能忍受；害是對有情心無悲愍、加以逼惱。論中說「瞋、害別相，准善應說」——比照無瞋（與樂）與不害（拔苦）：瞋障慈，害障悲。

**修行意義**：辨認出自己此刻是「忿」還是「恨」，就能對症：忿需當下的忍，恨需放下的慈，嫉需隨喜，害需悲心。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**One root**: for all five the Cheng weishi lun says "it has a part of aversion as substance; apart from aversion it has no characteristic or function". They are minor secondary afflictions, arising separately and "definitely designated" — names for aversion's face in particular situations.

**A time sequence: wrath → resentment → spite.** Anger erupting now is wrath; lingering after it, resentment; brooding over old grievances until they burst out in cruel words, spite.

**Different objects: jealousy and harmfulness.** Jealousy cannot bear others' success; harmfulness torments beings for lack of compassion. The treatise says their distinction from aversion "follows the wholesome": as non-hatred gives happiness and non-harming removes suffering, aversion obstructs loving-kindness and harmfulness obstructs compassion.

**For practice**: recognizing whether one is in wrath or resentment tells one the remedy — patience in the moment for wrath, letting go through kindness for resentment, sympathetic joy for jealousy, compassion for harmfulness.

quotes.text: 此即瞋恚一分為體，離瞋無別忿相用故。
quotes.note_en: It has a part of aversion as its substance; apart from aversion there is no separate characteristic or function of wrath.

questions.q_zh: 依《成唯識論》，忿、恨、惱、嫉、害的共同體性是什麼？
questions.q_en: According to the Cheng weishi lun, what do wrath, resentment, spite, jealousy and harmfulness share as substance?
questions.explain_zh: 五者都是「瞋恚一分為體」。
questions.explain_en: All five have "a part of aversion" as substance.

questions.q_zh: 被人當眾羞辱，當下怒火中燒、想要動手——這是？
questions.q_en: Insulted in public, one flares up on the spot and wants to strike. This is…
questions.explain_zh: 「依對現前不饒益境，憤發為性……執杖為業。」
questions.explain_en: "Flaring up at a present unbeneficial object … taking up the stick."

questions.q_zh: 事隔多年，一想起那人就耿耿於懷、無法釋懷——這是？
questions.q_en: Years later, one still cannot let go whenever one thinks of that person. This is…
questions.explain_zh: 「由忿為先，懷惡不捨，結怨為性。」
questions.explain_en: "Preceded by wrath, holding on to malice, binding enmity."

questions.q_zh: 同事升職，自己心中酸楚、悶悶不樂——這是？
questions.q_en: A colleague is promoted and one feels sour and gloomy. This is…
questions.explain_zh: 嫉：「不耐他榮，妬忌為性……憂慼為業。」
questions.explain_en: Jealousy: "unable to bear others' glory … its function is gloom."

questions.q_zh: 慳也是瞋恚的一分。
questions.q_en: Stinginess is also a part of aversion.
questions.explain_zh: 慳與憍是「貪愛一分為體」。
questions.explain_en: Stinginess and haughtiness are parts of greed.

questions.q_zh: 「忿→恨→惱」的順序，最後的「惱」通常表現為？
questions.q_en: In the sequence wrath → resentment → spite, how does spite usually show itself?
questions.explain_zh: 惱「䖧螫為業」，《五蘊論》說「發暴惡言尤䖧為性」。
questions.explain_en: Spite "stings"; the Pañcaskandhaka: "uttering violent, abusive words".

comparisons.title_en: Form aggregate vs. visible-form base
comparisons.summary_zh: 色蘊是一切物質（五根、五境、無表色）；色處只是眼所見的顏色與形狀。色處是色蘊的一小部分。
comparisons.summary_en: The form aggregate is all matter (five faculties, five objects, unmanifest form); the visible-form base is only colour and shape seen by the eye — a small part of the form aggregate.

cells.en: Elements, five faculties, five objects, unmanifest form
Ten bases plus part of the dharma base

comparisons.explanation_zh:
同一個「色」字有廣狹二義。**色蘊**的「色」是 rūpa 最廣的意思——物質，《雜阿含經》：「諸所有色，一切四大及四大造色」。**色處**的「色」則是眼根的對象：「謂眼境界，顯色、形色及表色等」。

依《大乘五蘊論》，色蘊在十二處中攝十處（眼等五根、色等五境）及法處的一分（無表色）。所以問「色處屬哪一蘊」，答「色蘊」；問「色蘊是否等於色處」，答「否」。
comparisons.explanation_en:
The same word rūpa has a broad and a narrow sense. The **form aggregate** uses the broadest: matter — "all form, the four elements and form derived from them" (Saṃyuktāgama). The **visible-form base** is the object of the eye: "the domain of the eye — colour, shape, bodily expression".

Per the Pañcaskandhaka, the form aggregate covers ten of the twelve bases (five faculties, five objects) plus part of the dharma base (unmanifest form). So the visible-form base belongs to the form aggregate, but the aggregate is far more than that base.

quotes.text: 云何為色？謂眼境界，顯色、形色及表色等。
quotes.note_en: What is visible form? The domain of the eye — colour, shape, bodily expression and so on.

questions.q_zh: 耳根屬於下列哪一個？
questions.q_en: The ear faculty belongs to…
questions.explain_zh: 耳根是物質，屬色蘊；但不是眼所見的色處。
questions.explain_en: The ear faculty is matter (form aggregate), but not the visible-form base.

questions.q_zh: 色蘊就是色處。
questions.q_en: The form aggregate is the same as the visible-form base.
questions.explain_zh: 色處只是色蘊的一部分。
questions.explain_en: The visible-form base is only part of the form aggregate.

questions.q_zh: 色處包括哪些？
questions.q_en: What does the visible-form base include?
questions.explain_zh: 「謂眼境界，顯色、形色及表色等。」
questions.explain_en: "The domain of the eye — colour, shape, expression."

comparisons.title_en: Calm, insight, concentration, meditative absorption
comparisons.summary_zh: 定是心所（專注）；止是以定為核心的修習；觀是以慧為核心的修習；禪（dhyāna）是特定的深定狀態（四禪）。惛沈障觀，掉舉障止。
comparisons.summary_en: Concentration is a mental factor (focus); calm is the practice centred on it; insight is the practice centred on wisdom; dhyāna is a specific class of deep absorptions. Torpor blocks insight, restlessness blocks calm.
comparisons.explanation_zh:
《雜阿含經》：「修習於止，終成於觀；修習觀已，亦成於止。」止觀相輔：止讓心穩，觀讓心明。

《成唯識論》精確指出障礙：掉舉「能障行捨、奢摩他」，惛沈「能障輕安、毘鉢舍那」。
comparisons.explanation_en:
Saṃyuktāgama: "Cultivating calm culminates in insight; having cultivated insight, calm is also accomplished." Calm steadies, insight clarifies.

The Cheng weishi lun names the obstacles precisely: restlessness "obstructs equanimity and śamatha", torpor "obstructs pliancy and vipaśyanā".

quotes.text: 『修習於止，多修習已，當何所成，修習於觀，多修習已，當何所成？』上座答言：尊者阿難！修習於止，終成於觀，修習觀已，亦成於止。
quotes.note_en: Cultivating calm culminates in insight; having cultivated insight, calm is also accomplished.

questions.q_zh: 觀（毘鉢舍那）的主要障礙是？
questions.q_en: What chiefly obstructs insight (vipaśyanā)?
questions.explain_zh: 惛沈「能障輕安、毘鉢舍那」。
questions.explain_en: Torpor "obstructs pliancy and vipaśyanā".

questions.q_zh: 定（samādhi）本身是一個心所。
questions.q_en: Samādhi itself is a mental factor.
questions.explain_zh: 定屬五別境心所之一。
questions.explain_en: It is one of the five object-specific factors.

questions.q_zh: 觀的核心心所是？
questions.q_en: The core mental factor of insight is…
questions.explain_zh: 止以定為核心，觀以慧為核心。
questions.explain_en: Calm centres on concentration, insight on wisdom.

comparisons.title_en: Saṃskāra vs. cetanā — and the three senses of 行
comparisons.summary_zh: 思是行蘊中「最勝」的一個心所，但行蘊不等於思；十二因緣的「行」是思所發動的業；「諸行」則是一切有為法。
comparisons.summary_en: Volition is the foremost single factor within the formations aggregate, but the aggregate is not volition; the saṃskāra of the twelve links is karma set in motion by volition; "all saṃskāras" means all conditioned things.

cells.zh: 受、想以外的一切心所＋心不相應行（百法中 49＋24＝73 法）
cells.en: All mental factors except feeling & perception + non-associated formations (49 + 24 = 73 in Yogācāra)

cells.zh: 「思謂令心造作為性」（成唯識論）

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**一、思是行蘊的「代表」，不是「全部」。** 《雜阿含經》以「六思身」定義行蘊，容易讓人以為行蘊＝思。但阿毗達磨指出：行蘊涵蓋受、想以外的所有心所（如信、貪、念、慧……）以及心不相應行（如得、命根、生、住、異、滅）。佛只舉「思」，是舉其最勝：「行名造作，思是業性造作義強，故為最勝」（《俱舍論》）。

**二、層次不同。** 思是一個具體的法（dharma）；行蘊是一個分類（蘊＝聚）。思必定屬於行蘊，但行蘊中的大多數法都不是思。

**三、遍行與業。** 思是遍行，每一念心都有；同時思是業的本體（「思即是意業」）。所以每一念心都帶有業性的造作傾向——這正是行蘊以「造作」為名的原因。

**四、與十二因緣之「行」。** 十二因緣的「行」是身、口、意三業，由思發動：意業就是思本身，身語業是「思已業」。行蘊描述的是當下這一念心的構成要素；十二因緣的行則是作為招感今生之因的過去業。

**五、諸行：最廣義。** 「諸行無常」的「行」＝一切有為法，連色、受、想、識都包括在內；它與「有為」（saṃskṛta，被造作的）同根。

**口訣**：思是將軍（一個心所）；行蘊是軍隊（除受、想外所有心所與不相應行）；十二因緣的行是打過的仗（已造的業）；諸行是整個被造作的世界。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**1. Volition represents the formations aggregate; it is not the whole of it.** Because the Saṃyuktāgama defines the aggregate as "the six classes of volition", it is easy to think saṃskāra-skandha = cetanā. But Abhidharma points out that the aggregate contains every mental factor apart from feeling and perception (faith, greed, mindfulness, wisdom…) plus the non-associated formations (acquisition, life-faculty, arising, duration, decay, cessation). The Buddha names volition as the foremost: "saṃskāra means forming; volition, being of the nature of karma, is strongest in forming — hence foremost" (Abhidharmakośa).

**2. Different levels.** Cetanā is one specific dharma; the formations aggregate is a category ("heap"). Volition always belongs to the formations aggregate, but most dharmas in that aggregate are not volition.

**3. Omnipresent and karmic.** Volition is omnipresent — in every moment of mind — and it is also the essence of karma ("volition is mental karma"). So every moment of mind carries a karmic, forming tendency; this is why the aggregate is named "forming".

**4. The saṃskāra of the twelve links** is bodily, verbal and mental karma, set in motion by volition: mental karma is volition itself, bodily and verbal karma are "karma after having willed". The aggregate describes the components of a present moment of mind; the second link describes past karma as the cause projecting this life.

**5. "All saṃskāras" — the widest sense.** In "all saṃskāras are impermanent", saṃskāra = every conditioned dharma, including form, feeling, perception and consciousness; it shares its root with saṃskṛta, "that which is formed".

**Mnemonic**: volition is the general (one factor); the formations aggregate is the army (every factor except feeling and perception, plus the non-associated formations); the second link is the battles already fought (karma done); all saṃskāras is the whole world that has been built.

quotes.text: 然薄伽梵於契經中說六思身為行蘊者，由最勝故。所以者何？行名造作，思是業性造作義強，故為最勝。
quotes.note_en: The Blessed One described the formations aggregate in the sūtra as the six classes of volition because volition is foremost. Why? Saṃskāra means "forming"; volition, being of the nature of karma, is strongest in forming — therefore foremost.

quotes.text: 世別由業生，思及思所作，思即是意業，所作謂身語。
quotes.note_en: The variety of the world is born of karma — volition and what volition produces. Volition is mental karma; what it produces is bodily and verbal karma.

questions.q_zh: 《雜阿含經》以「六思身」定義行蘊。《俱舍論》如何解釋？
questions.q_en: The Saṃyuktāgama defines the formations aggregate as "the six classes of volition". How does the Abhidharmakośa explain this?

options.en: The aggregate consists of volition alone

options.zh: 思在行蘊諸法中造作義最強，故舉思為代表
options.en: Volition is strongest in "forming" among its members, so it is named as representative
The other mental factors belong to the feeling aggregate

questions.explain_zh: 「行名造作，思是業性造作義強，故為最勝。」行蘊實際包括色受想識以外的一切有為法。
questions.explain_en: "Saṃskāra means forming; volition … is strongest in forming, hence foremost." The aggregate actually includes all conditioned dharmas other than form, feeling, perception and consciousness.

questions.q_zh: 行蘊就等於「思」這一個心所。
questions.q_en: The formations aggregate is the same as the single mental factor volition.
questions.explain_zh: 思只是行蘊中最勝的一法。唯識百法中行蘊攝 49 個心所與 24 個不相應行。
questions.explain_en: Volition is only the foremost member. In the hundred dharmas the aggregate contains 49 mental factors and 24 non-associated formations.

questions.q_zh: 在唯識百法中，「思」屬於行蘊。
questions.q_en: In the Yogācāra hundred dharmas, volition belongs to the formations aggregate.
questions.explain_zh: 行蘊＝除受、想外的一切心所＋不相應行；思是心所而不是受、想，所以屬行蘊。
questions.explain_en: Formations = all mental factors except feeling and perception, plus non-associated formations; volition is such a factor.

questions.q_zh: 「緣無明行」的「行」指什麼？
questions.q_en: In "ignorance conditions saṃskāra", what does saṃskāra mean?

options.en: All mental factors of the formations aggregate
The three kinds of karma — bodily, verbal, mental

questions.explain_zh: 《雜阿含經》第298經：「云何為行？行有三種——身行、口行、意行。」
questions.explain_en: SĀ 298: "What are formations? Formations are of three kinds — bodily, verbal and mental."

questions.q_zh: 「諸行無常」的「行」涵蓋什麼範圍？
questions.q_en: What does saṃskāra cover in "all saṃskāras are impermanent"?

options.zh: 一切有為法，包括色、受、想、行、識
options.en: All conditioned dharmas, including form, feeling, perception, formations, consciousness

questions.explain_zh: 諸行＝有為法。涅槃是無為法，不是「行」，故三法印說「一切行無常」而說「一切法無我」。
questions.explain_en: All saṃskāras = conditioned dharmas. Nirvāṇa is unconditioned, so the seals say "all saṃskāras are impermanent" but "all dharmas are non-self".

questions.q_zh: 依唯識，下列哪一個**不**屬於行蘊？
questions.q_en: In Yogācāra, which of these does NOT belong to the formations aggregate?
questions.explain_zh: 受自成受蘊。信是善心所、命根是心不相應行，都屬行蘊。
questions.explain_en: Feeling forms its own aggregate. Faith (a wholesome factor) and life-faculty (a non-associated formation) are in the formations aggregate.

questions.q_zh: 唯識百法中，行蘊共攝多少法？
questions.q_en: How many of the hundred dharmas does the formations aggregate contain?
questions.explain_zh: 51 心所減去受、想＝49，加上 24 個心不相應行＝73。（94 是五蘊總攝的有為法數。）
questions.explain_en: 51 mental factors minus feeling and perception = 49, plus 24 non-associated formations = 73. (94 is the total of conditioned dharmas in all five aggregates.)

questions.q_zh: 「思」只在有意識地做決定時才生起。
questions.q_en: Volition arises only when one consciously makes a decision.
questions.explain_zh: 思是遍行心所，「一切心中定可得」——每一念心都有思。
questions.explain_en: Volition is omnipresent — found in every moment of mind.

questions.q_zh: 依《俱舍論》，身業、語業屬於二業中的哪一種？
questions.q_en: According to the Abhidharmakośa, bodily and verbal karma belong to which of the two karmas?
questions.explain_zh: 「思已業者謂思所作。」意業即思本身（思業）；身、語業是思所發動（思已業）。
questions.explain_en: "Karma after having willed is what volition produces." Mental karma is volition itself; bodily and verbal karma are produced by it.

questions.q_zh: 南傳阿毗達摩的行蘊（saṅkhārakkhandha）包括多少個心所？
questions.q_en: How many cetasikas make up the saṅkhārakkhandha in Theravāda Abhidhamma?
questions.explain_zh: 南傳立 52 心所，除受、想外的 50 個構成行蘊。
questions.explain_en: Theravāda has 52 cetasikas; the 50 other than feeling and perception form the formations aggregate.

comparisons.title_en: Aggregates, bases, elements — the three analyses
comparisons.summary_zh: 五蘊、十二處、十八界是分析一切法的三種方式，分別針對三種我執：一性我執、受者我執、作者我執。蘊只攝有為法，處與界攝一切法。
comparisons.summary_en: The five aggregates, twelve bases and eighteen elements are three ways of analysing all dharmas, each countering a kind of self-grasping — as a unity, as an experiencer, as an agent. Aggregates cover only the conditioned; bases and elements cover everything.

cells.en: All dharmas (unconditioned in the dharma base)
All dharmas (unconditioned in the dharma element)

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**為何要三種說法**：《大乘五蘊論》：「為欲對治三種我執……謂一性我執、受者我執、作者我執。」把「我」拆成五堆，破「我是一個整體」；指出經驗只是根境相對，破「有個受用者」；指出認識只是根、境、識各持自性的組合，破「有個作者」。

**字義**：《俱舍論》頌：「聚、生門、種族，是蘊、處、界義。」

**互相攝**：《大乘五蘊論》：「色蘊即十處十界及法處法界（一分），識蘊即意處及七心界，餘三蘊及色蘊一分并諸無為即法處法界。」
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Why three**: Pañcaskandhaka: "To counteract three kinds of self-grasping — grasping a unitary self, an experiencer and an agent." Breaking the self into five heaps undoes "I am one whole"; showing experience as faculty meeting object undoes "someone enjoys it"; showing cognition as faculty, object and consciousness each holding its own nature undoes "someone does it".

**Meanings**: Abhidharmakośa verse: "Heap, gateway of arising, lineage — these are the meanings of aggregate, base and element."

**Mapping**: Pañcaskandhaka: "The form aggregate is ten bases and ten elements plus part of the dharma base and element; the consciousness aggregate is the mind base and the seven mind elements; the other three aggregates, part of form and all the unconditioned are the dharma base and element."

quotes.text: 為欲對治三種我執。如其次第三種我執者，謂一性我執、受者我執、作者我執。
quotes.note_en: In order to counteract three kinds of self-grasping — namely, grasping at a unitary self, at an experiencer, and at an agent.

quotes.text: 聚生門種族，是蘊處界義。
quotes.note_en: Heap, gateway of arising, lineage — these are the meanings of aggregate, base and element.

questions.q_zh: 哪一種分類只攝有為法，不攝無為法？
questions.q_en: Which analysis covers only conditioned dharmas?
questions.explain_zh: 無為法在法處、法界中，不在五蘊之內。
questions.explain_en: The unconditioned is in the dharma base and element, not in the aggregates.

questions.q_zh: 依《大乘五蘊論》，十八界主要對治哪一種我執？
questions.q_en: According to the Pañcaskandhaka, the eighteen elements chiefly counter which self-grasping?
questions.explain_zh: 「如其次第」：蘊—一性，處—受者，界—作者。
questions.explain_en: In order: aggregates — unity; bases — experiencer; elements — agent.

questions.q_zh: 「處」的字義是？
questions.q_en: What does āyatana mean?
questions.explain_zh: 「諸識生長門義，是處義。」
questions.explain_en: "The gateway where consciousnesses grow — that is the meaning of base."

questions.q_zh: 五蘊中的識蘊，在十八界中對應意界與六識界共七界。
questions.q_en: The consciousness aggregate corresponds to seven elements — the mind element and the six consciousness elements.
questions.explain_zh: 「識蘊即意處及七心界。」
questions.explain_en: "The consciousness aggregate is the mind base and the seven mind elements."

comparisons.title_en: Mindfulness, right mindfulness and forgetfulness
comparisons.summary_zh: 念是別境心所，明記曾習之境；「不忘念即是正念」；與煩惱相應、忘失所緣的則是隨煩惱「失念」（被偷走的念）。
comparisons.summary_en: Mindfulness is an object-specific factor that clearly keeps familiar objects in mind; "non-forgetful mindfulness is right mindfulness"; mindfulness bound up with afflictions, losing its object, is the secondary affliction "forgetfulness" (stolen mindfulness).

cells.en: Obstructs right mindfulness; basis of distraction

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**一條鏈**：念 → 定 → 慧。念是「定依」，定是「智依」。失念則反過來：失念 → 散亂 → 惡慧（散亂是「惡慧所依」）。一正一反，道出修行的心理機制。

**念本身通善惡**：百法把念放在別境而不是善心所，因為記住一件事本身無所謂善惡——念念不忘仇恨，也是一種「念」。《成唯識論》說「不忘念者，即是正念」，這是念在善品中的形態。

**失念的體性**：論中三說——念一分、癡一分、俱一分；《大乘五蘊論》直接稱之為「染污念」。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**A chain**: mindfulness → concentration → wisdom. Mindfulness is "the support of concentration", concentration "the support of wisdom". Forgetfulness runs the other way: forgetfulness → distraction → wrong discernment (distraction is "the basis of wrong discernment"). Together they lay bare the psychology of practice.

**Mindfulness itself is morally variable**: the hundred dharmas place it among the object-specific, not the wholesome, factors, because remembering is in itself neither good nor bad — never forgetting a grudge is also "mindfulness". "Non-forgetful mindfulness is right mindfulness" is its wholesome form.

**Substance of forgetfulness**: three views — part of mindfulness, part of delusion, part of both; the Pañcaskandhaka calls it "defiled mindfulness".

quotes.text: 不忘念者，即是正念。
quotes.note_en: Non-forgetful mindfulness is right mindfulness.

quotes.text: 云何失念？於諸所緣，不能明記為性；能障正念、散亂所依為業。
quotes.note_en: What is forgetfulness? Its nature is being unable to remember objects clearly; its function is to obstruct right mindfulness and be the basis of distraction.

questions.q_zh: 念的「業」（作用）是？
questions.q_en: What is the function of mindfulness?
questions.explain_zh: 念「定依為業」；定「智依為業」；欲「勤依為業」。
questions.explain_en: Mindfulness supports concentration; concentration supports wisdom; aspiration supports effort.

questions.q_zh: 失念是什麼的所依？
questions.q_en: Forgetfulness is the basis of…
questions.explain_zh: 失念「能障正念、散亂所依為業」。
questions.explain_en: Forgetfulness "obstructs right mindfulness and is the basis of distraction".

questions.q_zh: 在百法中，「念」屬於善心所。
questions.q_en: In the hundred dharmas, mindfulness is a wholesome factor.
questions.explain_zh: 念屬別境，通善惡；其善的形態是正念。
questions.explain_en: Mindfulness is object-specific and morally variable; its wholesome form is right mindfulness.

questions.q_zh: 梵語 muṣitasmṛtitā 的字面意思是？
questions.q_en: What does muṣitasmṛtitā literally mean?
questions.explain_zh: muṣita 意為「被偷」。
questions.explain_en: Muṣita means "stolen".

comparisons.title_en: Contact (sparśa) vs. the tangible (spraṣṭavya)
comparisons.summary_zh: 兩者漢譯都是「觸」：觸心所是根、境、識三和合的心理作用（行蘊）；觸境是身根所觸的對象，是色法（色蘊）。
comparisons.summary_en: Both are 觸 in Chinese: contact is the mental factor of faculty, object and consciousness meeting (formations aggregate); the tangible is the object of the body faculty, a form of matter (form aggregate).

cells.zh: 根境識三和，令心心所觸境
cells.en: Meeting of three; brings mind to its object

cells.zh: 四大及滑澀輕重冷飢渴等
cells.en: Elements, smooth, rough, heavy, light, cold, hunger, thirst

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**同字異義**：觸心所是 sparśa（「接觸」的作用），觸境是 spraṣṭavya（「應被觸的」東西）。

**範圍大不同**：觸心所伴隨每一念心，眼見色時有「眼觸」，意想法時有「意觸」——十二因緣的「觸」支就是這六觸。觸境則只是身根的對象，是五境之一。

**判斷方法**：看上下文——說「三事和合觸」「觸緣受」時是心所；說「色、聲、香、味、觸」時是觸境。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Same character, different words**: contact is sparśa (the act of contact); the tangible is spraṣṭavya ("what is to be touched").

**Very different scope**: contact accompanies every moment of mind — seeing forms there is eye-contact, thinking there is mind-contact; the link "contact" of the twelve is these six contacts. The tangible is only the object of the body faculty, one of the five sense objects.

**How to tell**: read the context — "the meeting of three is contact", "contact conditions feeling" means the mental factor; "form, sound, smell, taste, touch" means the tangible.

quotes.text: 『觸』謂三和分別變異，令心、心所觸境為性，受、想、思等所依為業。
quotes.note_en: Contact is the concurrence of the three with modification; its nature is to bring mind and mental factors into contact with the object; its function is to be the support of feeling, perception, volition and so on.

quotes.text: 言觸處者，謂四大種及前所說所觸一分。
quotes.note_en: The tangible base means the four great elements and the part of the tangible described before.

questions.q_zh: 「十二因緣」中的觸支，指的是？
questions.q_en: The "contact" of the twelve links refers to…

options.en: the mental factor (six classes of contact)

questions.explain_zh: 「云何為觸？謂六觸身——眼觸身……意觸身。」
questions.explain_en: "What is contact? The six classes — eye-contact … mind-contact."

questions.q_zh: 觸境屬於哪一蘊？
questions.q_en: Which aggregate does the tangible belong to?
questions.explain_zh: 觸境是色法，屬色蘊；觸心所屬行蘊。
questions.explain_en: The tangible is matter (form); contact is in formations.

questions.q_zh: 眼見色時也有「觸」心所生起。
questions.q_en: When the eye sees a form, the mental factor contact also arises.
questions.explain_zh: 觸是遍行，「緣眼、色，生眼識，三事和合觸」。
questions.explain_en: Contact is omnipresent — "eye, form, eye-consciousness: the meeting of three is contact".

comparisons.title_zh: 惛沈、掉舉與睡眠——禪修的兩大障礙
comparisons.title_en: Torpor, restlessness and sleep — the two great obstacles in meditation
comparisons.summary_zh: 惛沈令心下沉，障輕安與「觀」；掉舉令心上浮，障行捨與「止」。睡眠是身不自在、心昧略的狀態（不定心所），散亂則是在對象間流蕩。
comparisons.summary_en: Torpor makes the mind sink, obstructing pliancy and insight; restlessness makes it float, obstructing equanimity and calm. Sleep is a dim, contracted state (indeterminate); distraction is drifting between objects.

cells.en: Dim and contracted; body not under control

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**一沉一浮**：禪修時心最常出的兩種毛病，一是「沉」——昏昏沉沉，心提不起來；一是「浮」——念頭紛飛，心靜不下來。前者是惛沈，後者是掉舉。《成唯識論》精確地指出它們各自所障：惛沈「能障輕安、毘鉢舍那」，掉舉「能障行捨、奢摩他」。所以止（śamatha）怕掉舉，觀（vipaśyanā）怕惛沈。

**善心所的對治**：善心所中恰有一對針對它們——輕安「對治惛沈」，行捨「對治掉舉」。

**睡眠不是惛沈**：兩者合為五蓋中的「惛沈睡眠蓋」，但惛沈是遍一切染心的大隨煩惱；睡眠則是不定心所，是「身不自在、心極闇劣」的特殊狀態。

**掉舉不是散亂**：論中說「彼令易解，此令易緣」——掉舉是在理解上浮動，散亂是在對象上轉換。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Sinking and floating**: the two commonest faults in meditation are "sinking" — dull, unable to lift the mind — and "floating" — thoughts flying, unable to settle. The first is torpor, the second restlessness. The Cheng weishi lun is precise about what each obstructs: torpor "obstructs pliancy and vipaśyanā", restlessness "obstructs equanimity and śamatha". So calm fears restlessness, insight fears torpor.

**Wholesome antidotes**: the wholesome factors include a matching pair — pliancy "counteracts torpor", equanimity "counteracts restlessness".

**Sleep is not torpor**: together they form the hindrance "torpor and sleep", but torpor is a major secondary affliction in every defiled mind, whereas sleep is an indeterminate factor, a special state in which "the body is not free and the mind extremely dark and weak".

**Restlessness is not distraction**: "the former makes [the mind] change its understanding, the latter its object".

quotes.text: 云何掉舉？令心於境不寂靜為性；能障行捨、奢摩他為業。
quotes.note_en: What is restlessness? Its nature is making the mind not calm with regard to its object; its function is to obstruct equanimity and śamatha.

quotes.text: 云何惛沈？令心於境，無堪任為性；能障輕安、毘鉢舍那為業。
quotes.note_en: What is torpor? Its nature is making the mind unfit with regard to its object; its function is to obstruct pliancy and vipaśyanā.

questions.q_zh: 依《成唯識論》，惛沈障礙的是？
questions.q_en: According to the Cheng weishi lun, torpor obstructs…
questions.explain_zh: 惛沈「能障輕安、毘鉢舍那為業」。
questions.explain_en: Torpor "obstructs pliancy and vipaśyanā".

questions.q_zh: 對治掉舉的善心所是？
questions.q_en: Which wholesome factor counteracts restlessness?
questions.explain_zh: 行捨「對治掉舉，靜住為業」。
questions.explain_en: Equanimity "counteracts restlessness, bringing quiet abiding".

questions.q_zh: 睡眠和惛沈一樣，都是大隨煩惱。
questions.q_en: Like torpor, sleep is a major secondary affliction.
questions.explain_zh: 睡眠是不定心所，可善可惡；惛沈才是大隨煩惱。
questions.explain_en: Sleep is indeterminate; only torpor is a major secondary affliction.

questions.q_zh: 打坐時心中不斷浮現昨天的快樂事，無法平靜——主要是？
questions.q_en: While sitting, memories of yesterday's pleasures keep bubbling up and the mind cannot settle. Chiefly…
questions.explain_zh: 掉舉令心不寂靜，論中一說「此由憶昔樂事生故」。
questions.explain_en: Restlessness makes the mind unsettled; one view says it "arises from recalling past pleasures".

questions.q_zh: 掉舉與散亂的區別，《成唯識論》如何說？
questions.q_en: How does the Cheng weishi lun distinguish restlessness from distraction?

options.zh: 掉舉令易解，散亂令易緣
options.en: restlessness changes understanding; distraction changes object

options.zh: 掉舉令易緣，散亂令易解
options.en: restlessness changes object; distraction changes understanding

questions.explain_zh: 「掉舉、散亂二用何別？彼令易解，此令易緣。」
questions.explain_en: "The former makes [the mind] change its understanding, the latter its object."

comparisons.title_en: Emptiness vs. non-self
comparisons.summary_zh: 早期經典的無我主要破「人我」；大乘的空進一步說一切法（包括構成人的諸法）都無自性——人無我加上法無我。
comparisons.summary_en: Early non-self chiefly undoes the personal self; Mahāyāna emptiness extends this to all dharmas, including those composing the person — selflessness of persons plus of phenomena.

cells.zh: 色無常，無常即苦，苦即非我

cells.en: Form is emptiness, emptiness is form

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**並非不同的真理**：無我與空都源於緣起。早期經典也說「空」（如「空三昧」），大乘經典也說「無我」；差別主要在範圍：阿毗達磨分析出的諸法是否也無自性。

**大乘的推進**：《心經》說五蘊皆空；《百法明門論》結尾說「一補特伽羅無我、二法無我」。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Not different truths**: both derive from dependent origination. Early texts also speak of emptiness (e.g. the emptiness concentration), and Mahāyāna texts of non-self; the difference is mainly scope — whether the dharmas found by Abhidharma analysis also lack own-being.

**The Mahāyāna step**: the Heart Sūtra declares the five aggregates empty; the Hundred Dharmas treatise ends with "non-self of the person and non-self of dharmas".

quotes.text: 色不異空，空不異色，色即是空，空即是色；
quotes.note_en: Form is not other than emptiness; emptiness is not other than form. Form is emptiness; emptiness is form.

questions.q_zh: 大乘在「人無我」之外，特別強調的是？
questions.q_en: Beyond selflessness of persons, the Mahāyāna stresses…
questions.explain_zh: 二無我：人無我、法無我。
questions.explain_en: Two selflessnesses: of persons and of phenomena.

questions.q_zh: 空的意思是「什麼都不存在」。
questions.q_en: Emptiness means "nothing exists at all".
questions.explain_zh: 空是無自性，不是斷滅；「以有空義故，一切法得成」。
questions.explain_en: Emptiness is lack of own-being, not nothingness.

comparisons.title_zh: 佛的三身：法身、報身、化身
comparisons.title_en: The three bodies — dharma, enjoyment, emanation
comparisons.summary_zh: 法身是真如本性（自性身），報身是福慧所成、受用法樂之身（受用身），化身是為度眾隨類示現之身（變化身）。
comparisons.summary_en: The dharma body is the nature of suchness; the enjoyment body is produced by merit and wisdom, enjoying the Dharma; the emanation body appears in forms suited to beings.

cells.en: Ordinary beings, two vehicles, pre-stage bodhisattvas

comparisons.explanation_zh: 《成唯識論》：「如是法身，有三相別：一、自性身……二、受用身……三、變化身。」三身不是三個佛，而是同一佛果的三個面向：真如本性、圓滿功德、應機示現。
comparisons.explanation_en: Cheng weishi lun: "This dharma body has three aspects: the intrinsic body, the enjoyment body and the transformation body." They are not three buddhas but three aspects of one buddhahood: the nature of suchness, perfect qualities, and manifestation suited to beings.

quotes.text: 三、變化身：謂諸如來由成事智，變現無量隨類化身，居淨、穢土，為未登地諸菩薩眾、二乘、異生，稱彼機宜，現通說法，令各獲得諸利樂事。
quotes.note_en: Third, the emanation body — through the wisdom that accomplishes tasks, the tathāgatas manifest countless emanations suited to kinds of beings, in pure and impure lands, teaching according to their capacities so that each gains benefit and happiness.

questions.q_zh: 歷史上的釋迦牟尼佛屬於哪一身？
questions.q_en: The historical Śākyamuni is which body?
questions.explain_zh: 為凡夫二乘示現出生成道的是化身（變化身）。
questions.explain_en: The body displaying birth and awakening for ordinary beings is the emanation body.

questions.q_zh: 唯識稱法身為？
questions.q_en: Yogācāra calls the dharma body…
questions.explain_zh: 「一、自性身……亦名法身。」
questions.explain_en: "The intrinsic body … is also called the dharma body."

comparisons.title_en: The three seals — impermanence, non-self, nirvāṇa
comparisons.summary_zh: 諸行無常（只說有為）、諸法無我（通有為無為）、涅槃寂靜（無為）。「行」與「法」的用字差別是理解關鍵。
comparisons.summary_en: All saṃskāras are impermanent (conditioned only), all dharmas are non-self (conditioned and unconditioned), nirvāṇa is peace (unconditioned). The switch from "saṃskāra" to "dharma" is the key.
comparisons.explanation_zh:
《大智度論》：「佛法印有三種：一者、一切有為法念念生滅皆無常，二者、一切法無我，三者、寂滅涅槃。」

**為什麼第一印說「行」，第二印說「法」**？涅槃是無為法，不生不滅，所以不是無常；但涅槃也不是「我」。所以無常只能說「諸行」，無我則可以說「諸法」。

**推理鏈**：《雜阿含經》：「色無常，無常即苦，苦即非我。」南傳常把「苦」列入而說三相（無常、苦、無我）；北傳的三法印則以涅槃寂靜為第三。
comparisons.explanation_en:
Dazhidu lun: "The seals of the Buddha's Dharma are three: all conditioned dharmas arise and cease moment by moment and are impermanent; all dharmas are non-self; nirvāṇa is peace."

**Why "saṃskāras" in the first and "dharmas" in the second?** Nirvāṇa is unconditioned — unarisen, unceasing — so not impermanent; yet it is not a self either. Impermanence can be said only of saṃskāras; non-self of all dharmas.

**The reasoning**: Saṃyuktāgama: "Form is impermanent; the impermanent is suffering; suffering is not self." Theravāda lists "three characteristics" with suffering as the second; the northern "three seals" end with nirvāṇa.

quotes.text: 何等是佛法印？答曰：佛法印有三種：一者、一切有為法念念生滅皆無常，二者、一切法無我，三者、寂滅涅槃。
quotes.note_en: What are the seals of the Buddha's Dharma? Three — all conditioned dharmas arise and cease moment by moment and are impermanent; all dharmas are non-self; nirvāṇa is peace.

questions.q_zh: 涅槃也是無常的。
questions.q_en: Nirvāṇa is also impermanent.
questions.explain_zh: 涅槃是無為法，不生不滅；無常只說有為（諸行）。
questions.explain_en: Nirvāṇa is unconditioned; impermanence applies only to saṃskāras.

questions.q_zh: 涅槃也是無我的。
questions.q_en: Nirvāṇa is also non-self.
questions.explain_zh: 「諸法無我」包括無為法。
questions.explain_en: "All dharmas are non-self" includes the unconditioned.

questions.q_zh: 《雜阿含經》的推理順序是？
questions.q_en: The reasoning order in the Saṃyuktāgama is…
questions.explain_zh: 「色無常，無常即苦，苦即非我。」
questions.explain_en: "Form is impermanent; the impermanent is suffering; suffering is not self."

comparisons.title_en: The three natures and three non-natures
comparisons.summary_zh: 遍計所執（如繩上見蛇，全無）、依他起（如繩，緣生幻有）、圓成實（如麻，真實本性）。依三性立三無性：相無性、生無性、勝義無性。
comparisons.summary_en: Imagined (the snake seen in a rope — nonexistent), dependent (the rope — conditioned, illusory existence), perfected (the hemp — the real nature). On them rest three non-natures: of characteristics, of arising, and ultimate.
comparisons.explanation_zh:
《唯識三十頌》：「由彼彼遍計，遍計種種物，此遍計所執，自性無所有。依他起自性，分別緣所生。圓成實於彼，常遠離前性。」

**關鍵**：三性不是三樣東西，而是同一現象的三個面向。依他起是基礎；在其上執著實我實法便是遍計所執；遠離這種執著所顯的真如便是圓成實。

**三無性**：「即依此三性，立彼三無性，故佛密意說，一切法無性。」般若經說「一切法無自性」，唯識解釋為依三性而說的密意，而不是一切皆無。
comparisons.explanation_en:
Thirty Verses: "Whatever is imagined by this or that imagining — this imagined nature has no existence. The dependent nature arises from conceptualization and conditions. The perfected is that [dependent] forever free of the former."

**Key point**: the three natures are not three things but three aspects of the same phenomenon. The dependent is the basis; grasping it as real self and dharmas is the imagined; the suchness revealed when that grasping is removed is the perfected.

**Three non-natures**: "Based on these three natures the three non-natures are established; thus the Buddha, with hidden intention, taught that all dharmas are without nature." Yogācāra reads the Prajñāpāramitā's "no own-being" as intended in this sense, not as "nothing exists".

quotes.text: 由彼彼遍計，遍計種種物，此遍計所執，自性無所有。依他起自性，分別緣所生。圓成實於彼，常遠離前性。
quotes.note_en: Whatever is imagined by this or that imagining, of various things — this imagined nature has no existence. The dependent nature arises from conceptualization and conditions. The perfected is that forever free of the former.

questions.q_zh: 在繩蛇喻中，「繩」比喻哪一性？
questions.q_en: In the rope-snake simile, the rope stands for…
questions.explain_zh: 蛇是遍計所執，繩是依他起，麻是圓成實。
questions.explain_en: Snake — imagined; rope — dependent; hemp — perfected.

questions.q_zh: 依他起性上立哪一種無性？
questions.q_en: Which non-nature is based on the dependent nature?
questions.explain_zh: 依他起非自然生，故立生無性。
questions.explain_en: The dependent does not arise by itself — non-nature of arising.

questions.q_zh: 圓成實性是依他起性以外的另一種實體。
questions.q_en: The perfected nature is a separate entity apart from the dependent nature.
questions.explain_zh: 圓成實是依他起遠離遍計所執所顯的真如，「於彼常遠離前性」。
questions.explain_en: It is the dependent, free of the imagined — "that forever free of the former".

comparisons.title_en: The three trainings — morality, concentration, wisdom
comparisons.summary_zh: 因戒生定，因定發慧。戒止粗惡、定息散亂、慧斷煩惱；三者次第相依。
comparisons.summary_en: From morality comes concentration, from concentration wisdom. Morality stops gross wrongdoing, concentration calms distraction, wisdom cuts off affliction — each supports the next.
comparisons.explanation_zh:
《雜阿含經》：「有三學……謂增上戒學、增上意學、增上慧學。」「增上意學」即定學。

**次第**：《遺教經》說「依因此戒，得生諸禪定及滅苦智慧」；心所上也是如此——念是「定依」，定是「智依」。戒使生活單純，心才能定；心定，才能如實觀察而生慧。

**六度的對應**：持戒、禪定、般若三度即三學；布施、忍辱、精進則是助成。
comparisons.explanation_en:
Saṃyuktāgama: "There are three trainings — higher morality, higher mind and higher wisdom"; "higher mind" is concentration.

**Sequence**: the Yijiao jing says that relying on morality one attains the meditations and the wisdom that ends suffering; the mental factors show the same chain — mindfulness supports concentration, concentration supports wisdom. Morality simplifies life so the mind can settle; a settled mind sees clearly and wisdom arises.

**In the six perfections**: morality, meditation and wisdom correspond to the three trainings; giving, patience and diligence support them.

quotes.text: 有三學。何等為三？謂增上戒學、增上意學、謂增上慧學。
quotes.note_en: There are three trainings. What are the three? Higher morality, higher mind and higher wisdom.

questions.q_zh: 「增上意學」是指？
questions.q_en: What is "higher mind" training?
questions.explain_zh: 增上意（心）學即定學。
questions.explain_en: Higher mind training is concentration.

questions.q_zh: 依心所的作用，定是什麼的所依？
questions.q_en: By the mental-factor functions, concentration is the support of…
questions.explain_zh: 定「智依為業」。
questions.explain_en: Concentration "supports wisdom".

comparisons.title_en: The three vehicles — disciple, solitary buddha, bodhisattva
comparisons.summary_zh: 聲聞聞法修四諦、自求涅槃；緣覺觀因緣、樂獨善寂；菩薩發菩提心、行六度、自利利他而成佛。
comparisons.summary_en: Disciples hear the teaching and seek nirvāṇa for themselves; solitary buddhas contemplate conditions and delight in solitude; bodhisattvas arouse the awakening mind, practise the perfections and become buddhas for all.

cells.en: Hearing the teaching; the noble truths

comparisons.explanation_zh: 《妙法蓮華經》火宅喻分別三乘：「欲速出三界，自求涅槃，是名聲聞乘」；「求自然慧，樂獨善寂，深知諸法因緣，是名辟支佛乘」；而求一切智、憐愍安樂無量眾生者，是名大乘。《法華經》最後說三乘是方便，終歸一佛乘。
comparisons.explanation_en: The Lotus Sūtra's burning-house parable distinguishes them: "wishing to leave the three realms quickly and seeking nirvāṇa for oneself — the disciple vehicle"; "seeking natural wisdom, delighting in solitary quiet, deeply knowing causes and conditions — the pratyekabuddha vehicle"; those seeking omniscience out of compassion for countless beings — the great vehicle. The sūtra finally presents the three as skilful means leading to the one buddha-vehicle.

quotes.text: 內有智性，從佛世尊聞法信受，慇懃精進，欲速出三界，自求涅槃，是名聲聞乘
quotes.note_en: Having inner wisdom, hearing the Dharma from the Buddha and accepting it, diligent, wishing to leave the three realms swiftly and seeking nirvāṇa for oneself — this is the disciple vehicle.

questions.q_zh: 「樂獨善寂，深知諸法因緣」描述的是？
questions.q_en: "Delighting in solitary quiet, deeply knowing causes and conditions" describes…
questions.explain_zh: 《法華經》：「……是名辟支佛乘。」
questions.explain_en: Lotus Sūtra: "… this is the pratyekabuddha vehicle."

questions.q_zh: 兼斷煩惱障與所知障的是？
questions.q_en: Who removes both obstructions?
questions.explain_zh: 二乘只斷煩惱障。
questions.explain_en: The two vehicles remove only the afflictive obstruction.

comparisons.title_en: Craving vs. clinging (tṛṣṇā & upādāna)
comparisons.summary_zh: 愛是渴求（想要），取是執取（抓住、追逐）；取是愛的增長。兩者都以貪為核心，而取還包括對見解、戒禁與「我」的執著。
comparisons.summary_en: Craving is thirst (wanting); clinging is seizing and pursuing — craving grown strong. Both centre on greed, and clinging also includes attachment to views, observances and a self.

cells.en: Greed for pleasures and sexual love

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**由渴到抓**：愛是內心的渴求；取是渴求增強後，向外追逐、緊抓不放。《俱舍論》說取是「為得諸境界，遍馳求」。

**取比愛多了「見」**：愛的三種都是對存在的貪；取的四種中，後三種（見取、戒取、我取）都涉及錯誤的見解——執著自己的見解、執著錯誤的修行方法、執著有我的學說。

**與貪的關係**：愛與取都是貪（及見）的表現，是十二因緣中「現在三因」的惑。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**From thirst to grasping**: craving is inner thirst; clinging is that thirst intensified into outward pursuit and tight holding. The Abhidharmakośa calls clinging "running about everywhere to obtain objects".

**Clinging adds views**: all three cravings are greed for existence; of the four clingings, three concern views — clinging to one's opinions, to wrong methods of practice, to doctrines of a self.

**Relation to greed**: both are expressions of greed (and views), the "affliction" among the three present causes of the twelve links.

quotes.text: 在婬愛前受，貪資具婬愛，為得諸境界，遍馳求名取
quotes.note_en: Before sexual love is feeling; greed for the means of pleasure and sexual love is craving; running about everywhere seeking to obtain objects is clinging.

questions.q_zh: 「見取、戒取」屬於哪一支的內容？
questions.q_en: Clinging to views and to rules belong to which link?
questions.explain_zh: 四取：欲取、見取、戒取、我取。
questions.explain_en: Four clingings: to sense pleasures, views, rules, self.

questions.q_zh: 《雜阿含經》所說三愛是？
questions.q_en: What are the three cravings in the Saṃyuktāgama?
questions.explain_zh: 「謂三愛——欲愛、色愛、無色愛。」
questions.explain_en: "The three cravings: for desire, for form, for the formless."

questions.q_zh: 取是愛的進一步增長。
questions.q_en: Clinging is craving grown stronger.
questions.explain_zh: 愛增長而四處追求、執取，即是取。
questions.explain_en: Craving intensified into pursuit and grasping is clinging.

comparisons.title_zh: 十二因緣的三世兩重因果
comparisons.title_en: The twelve links across three lives — two layers of cause and effect
comparisons.summary_zh: 說一切有部把十二支分配到過去、現在、未來三世：過去二因（無明、行）→ 現在五果（識至受）→ 現在三因（愛、取、有）→ 未來二果（生、老死）。
comparisons.summary_en: The Sarvāstivāda distributes the twelve links over three lives: two past causes (ignorance, formations) → five present effects (consciousness to feeling) → three present causes (craving, clinging, becoming) → two future effects (birth, ageing-and-death).

cells.en: consciousness, name-and-form, six bases, contact, feeling

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**三世**：《俱舍論》：「如是諸緣起，十二支三際，前後際各二，中八據圓滿。」前際（過去）二支，後際（未來）二支，中際（現在）八支。

**兩重因果**：過去的無明與行（惑、業）招感現在的識、名色、六入、觸、受五果；現在又起愛、取（惑）而造有（業），招感未來的生與老死。

**惑、業、苦**：無明、愛、取是惑；行、有是業；其餘七支是苦。惑生業，業生苦，苦中又起惑——輪迴如輪不息。

**修行的著力點**：受是過去業的果，無法改變；但「受緣愛」這一環可以斷——在受上不起愛，就不再造新的因。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Three lives**: Abhidharmakośa: "These twelve links of dependent origination span three periods: two each for the past and future, eight in the middle, [counted] at their fullest." Two links belong to the past, two to the future, eight to the present.

**Two layers of cause and effect**: past ignorance and formations (affliction, karma) bring the five present effects, consciousness through feeling; in the present, craving and clinging (affliction) produce becoming (karma), which brings future birth and ageing-and-death.

**Affliction, karma, suffering**: ignorance, craving and clinging are affliction; formations and becoming are karma; the other seven are suffering. Affliction produces karma, karma suffering, and within suffering affliction arises again — the wheel keeps turning.

**Where practice bites**: feeling is the result of past karma and cannot be changed; but the link "feeling → craving" can be cut — not craving at feeling, one creates no new causes.

quotes.text: 如是諸緣起，十二支三際，前後際各二，中八據圓滿。
quotes.note_en: These links of dependent origination, twelve in number, span three periods — two each in the former and latter periods, eight in the middle, counted at their fullest.

questions.q_zh: 依三世兩重因果，「行」屬於？
questions.q_en: In the three-life scheme, formations belong to…
questions.explain_zh: 過去二因：無明、行。
questions.explain_en: The two past causes: ignorance and formations.

questions.q_zh: 下列哪一支屬於「現在三因」？
questions.q_en: Which link is one of the three present causes?
questions.explain_zh: 現在三因：愛、取、有。
questions.explain_en: Present causes: craving, clinging, becoming.

questions.q_zh: 行與有都屬於「業」。
questions.q_en: Formations and becoming are both karma.
questions.explain_zh: 行是過去業，有是現在業。
questions.explain_en: Formations are past karma, becoming present karma.

questions.q_zh: 十二支中屬「惑」的是？
questions.q_en: Which links are "affliction"?
questions.explain_zh: 惑：無明、愛、取；業：行、有；其餘七支是苦。
questions.explain_en: Affliction: ignorance, craving, clinging; karma: formations, becoming; the other seven are suffering.

comparisons.title_en: Attainment of non-perception vs. attainment of cessation
comparisons.summary_zh: 兩者都是「無心定」：無想定是凡夫以出離想為目的所修，只滅前六識；滅盡定是聖者以止息為目的所入，連第七識的染污部分也滅。
comparisons.summary_en: Both are "mindless attainments": the non-perceptual one is practised by ordinary meditators seeking to escape perception and stops only the first six consciousnesses; cessation is entered by noble ones seeking stillness and also stops the defiled part of the seventh.

cells.zh: 前六識及恒行一分（第七染分）
cells.en: First six plus part of the constant (defiled seventh)

comparisons.explanation_zh:
《大乘五蘊論》分別定義：無想等至「由出離想作意為先，不恒現行心心法滅為性」；滅盡等至「由止息想作意為先，不恒現行及恒行一分心心法滅為性」。

兩者中阿賴耶識都不滅——這是唯識論證第八識的理由之一：出定時，心識從哪裡再生起？
comparisons.explanation_en:
The Pañcaskandhaka defines the non-perceptual attainment as "preceded by attention to escaping perception, the cessation of the non-constant minds and factors", and cessation as "preceded by attention to stilling, the cessation of the non-constant and part of the constant minds and factors".

In both, the store consciousness continues — one of Yogācāra's arguments for it: from where would mind re-arise on emerging?

quotes.text: 云何滅盡等至？謂已離無所有處貪，從第一有更求勝進，由止息想作意為先，不恒現行及恒行一分心心法滅為性。
quotes.note_en: What is the attainment of cessation? Free of desire for the sphere of nothingness, seeking to progress beyond the peak of existence, preceded by attention aimed at stilling, its nature is the cessation of the non-constant minds and mental factors and part of the constant ones.

questions.q_zh: 哪一種定連第七識的染污部分也滅？
questions.q_en: Which attainment also stops the defiled part of the seventh consciousness?
questions.explain_zh: 滅盡定滅「不恒現行及恒行一分」。
questions.explain_en: Cessation stops "the non-constant and part of the constant".

questions.q_zh: 在滅盡定中，阿賴耶識也滅了。
questions.q_en: In the attainment of cessation, the store consciousness also ceases.
questions.explain_zh: 阿賴耶恆轉不斷，執持根身。
questions.explain_en: The store consciousness continues, sustaining the body.

comparisons.title_en: Two graspings, two obstructions, two selflessnesses, two fruits
comparisons.summary_zh: 我執生煩惱障，證人無我而斷，得解脫（涅槃）；法執生所知障，證法無我而斷，得菩提。
comparisons.summary_en: Self-grasping produces the afflictive obstruction, cut by realizing selflessness of persons, yielding liberation; grasping at dharmas produces the cognitive obstruction, cut by realizing selflessness of phenomena, yielding awakening.
comparisons.explanation_zh:
《成唯識論》開卷即說：「由我、法執二障具生，若證二空，彼障隨斷。斷障為得二勝果故，由斷續生煩惱障故，證真解脫；由斷礙解所知障故，得大菩提。」整部論的目的，就是為了使人「於二空有迷謬者生正解」。

**名稱提醒**：所知障不是「知識的障礙」，而是「障礙所知境」的障。
comparisons.explanation_en:
The Cheng weishi lun opens: "From grasping at self and dharmas the two obstructions arise; realizing the two emptinesses, they are removed. They are cut to obtain two supreme fruits: cutting the afflictive obstruction that continues rebirth brings true liberation; cutting the cognitive obstruction that hinders understanding brings great awakening." The whole treatise aims to give right understanding to those confused about the two emptinesses.

**Name reminder**: 所知障 is not "obstruction by knowledge" but "obstruction to the knowable".

quotes.text: 由我、法執二障具生，若證二空，彼障隨斷。斷障為得二勝果故，由斷續生煩惱障故，證真解脫；由斷礙解所知障故，得大菩提。
quotes.note_en: From grasping at self and at dharmas the two obstructions arise; realizing the two emptinesses, they are removed. The obstructions are cut to gain two supreme fruits — cutting the afflictive obstruction that continues rebirth, one realizes true liberation; cutting the cognitive obstruction that hinders understanding, one attains great awakening.

questions.q_zh: 所知障由什麼而生？
questions.q_en: From what does the cognitive obstruction arise?
questions.explain_zh: 我執生煩惱障，法執生所知障。
questions.explain_en: Self-grasping → afflictive; dharma-grasping → cognitive.

questions.q_zh: 斷煩惱障所得的果是？
questions.q_en: Cutting the afflictive obstruction yields…
questions.explain_zh: 「由斷續生煩惱障故，證真解脫。」
questions.explain_en: "Cutting the afflictive obstruction … one realizes true liberation."

questions.q_zh: 阿羅漢已斷所知障。
questions.q_en: Arhats have cut the cognitive obstruction.
questions.explain_zh: 二乘斷煩惱障，未斷所知障。
questions.explain_en: The two vehicles cut the afflictive but not the cognitive obstruction.

comparisons.title_en: Conventional and ultimate truth
comparisons.summary_zh: 世俗諦是依名言約定成立的真實（有人、有物、有因果）；勝義諦是聖智所證的空性、真如。依世俗而證勝義，兩者不可偏廢。
comparisons.summary_en: Conventional truth is reality established by language and convention (persons, things, cause and effect); ultimate truth is the emptiness or suchness realized by noble wisdom. One reaches the ultimate through the conventional; neither can be discarded.

cells.en: Phenomena, cause and effect set up by convention

cells.zh: 第一義諦（羅什）、勝義諦（玄奘）

comparisons.explanation_zh:
《中論》：「諸佛依二諦，為眾生說法：一以世俗諦，二第一義諦。」「若不依俗諦，不得第一義；不得第一義，則不得涅槃。」

二諦不是兩個世界，而是同一實在的兩種觀看：從名言看，有人有法；從究竟看，一切無自性。
comparisons.explanation_en:
Mūlamadhyamakakārikā: "The buddhas teach relying on two truths: worldly conventional truth and ultimate truth." "Without relying on the conventional, the ultimate is not attained; without the ultimate, nirvāṇa is not attained."

The two truths are not two worlds but two ways of seeing one reality: conventionally there are persons and things; ultimately nothing has own-being.

quotes.text: 若不依俗諦，不得第一義；不得第一義，則不得涅槃。
quotes.note_en: Without relying on conventional truth, the ultimate is not attained; without attaining the ultimate, nirvāṇa is not attained.

questions.q_zh: 鳩摩羅什譯的「第一義諦」即？
questions.q_en: Kumārajīva's 第一義諦 corresponds to…
questions.explain_zh: 第一義諦＝勝義諦（paramārtha-satya）。
questions.explain_en: 第一義諦 = paramārtha-satya.

questions.q_zh: 依《中論》，不依世俗諦也能得到第一義。
questions.q_en: According to the Madhyamaka verses, the ultimate can be attained without relying on the conventional.
questions.explain_zh: 「若不依俗諦，不得第一義。」
questions.explain_en: "Without relying on the conventional, the ultimate is not attained."

comparisons.title_en: Three classes of secondary afflictions, real and designated
comparisons.summary_zh: 小隨十（各別起）、中隨二（遍不善心）、大隨八（遍一切染心）。小十與大隨中的放逸、失念、不正知定是假有；無慚、無愧、不信、懈怠定是實有；掉舉、惛沈、散亂有假實二說。
comparisons.summary_en: Ten minor (arise separately), two intermediate (in every unwholesome mind), eight major (in every defiled mind). The ten minor plus heedlessness, forgetfulness and non-alertness are definitely designated; lack of self-respect, lack of decorum, faithlessness and laziness definitely real; restlessness, torpor and distraction disputed.

cells.zh: 忿、恨、惱、覆、誑、諂、憍、害、嫉、慳
cells.en: wrath, resentment, spite, concealment, deceit, guile, haughtiness, harmfulness, jealousy, stinginess
lack of self-respect, lack of decorum

cells.zh: 掉舉、惛沈、不信、懈怠、放逸、失念、散亂、不正知
cells.en: restlessness, torpor, faithlessness, laziness, heedlessness, forgetfulness, distraction, non-alertness

cells.zh: 不信、懈怠實；放逸、失念、不正知假；掉舉、惛沈、散亂有二說
cells.en: Faithlessness, laziness real; heedlessness, forgetfulness, non-alertness designated; the other three disputed

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**為什麼叫「隨」煩惱**：《成唯識論》：「唯是煩惱分位差別、等流性故，名隨煩惱。」它們要嘛是根本煩惱在特定情境下的「分位」（如忿是瞋的分位），要嘛是根本煩惱的「等流」（同類延續）。

**三類的判準是「範圍」**：小隨煩惱各自生起，不會同時出現（忿時不一定有嫉）；中隨二者只要是不善心就一定有；大隨八者只要是染污心（包括有覆無記）就一定有。

**中隨 vs 大隨**：差別在「有覆無記心」——例如第七末那識的心是染污但屬無記，其中有大隨煩惱，卻沒有無慚、無愧。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Why "secondary"**: Cheng weishi lun: "They are only phases of the afflictions or outflows of the same kind, hence called secondary afflictions." They are either the root afflictions in particular situations (wrath is a phase of aversion) or their homogeneous continuations.

**The three classes are defined by scope**: minor ones arise separately, not together (wrath need not come with jealousy); the two intermediate ones are present whenever the mind is unwholesome; the eight major ones whenever it is defiled at all (including obscured-neutral minds).

**Intermediate vs major**: the difference shows in "obscured-neutral" minds — e.g. the seventh consciousness is defiled yet morally neutral; the major secondary afflictions accompany it, but not lack of self-respect and decorum.

quotes.text: 唯是煩惱分位差別、等流性，故名隨煩惱。此二十種，類別有三：謂忿等十，各別起故，名小隨煩惱；無慚等二，遍不善故，名中隨煩惱；掉舉等八，遍染心故，名大隨煩惱。
quotes.note_en: Being only phases of the afflictions and outflows of the same kind, they are called secondary afflictions. These twenty are of three classes — wrath and the rest, ten, arising separately, are called minor; the two beginning with lack of self-respect, pervading all unwholesome minds, intermediate; the eight beginning with restlessness, pervading all defiled minds, major.

quotes.text: 如是二十隨煩惱中，小十、大三，定是假有；無慚、無愧、不信、懈怠定是實有；教、理成故。掉舉、惛沈、散亂三種，有義是假，有義是實。
quotes.note_en: Among these twenty secondary afflictions, the ten minor and three of the major are definitely designated; lack of self-respect, lack of decorum, faithlessness and laziness are definitely real, as established by scripture and reasoning; restlessness, torpor and distraction — some say designated, some say real.

questions.q_zh: 無慚、無愧屬於哪一類？
questions.q_en: Lack of self-respect and decorum belong to which class?
questions.explain_zh: 「無慚等二，遍不善故，名中隨煩惱。」
questions.explain_en: "The two beginning with lack of self-respect pervade unwholesome minds: intermediate."

questions.q_zh: 大隨煩惱的判準是？
questions.q_en: What defines the major secondary afflictions?
questions.explain_zh: 「掉舉等八，遍染心故，名大隨煩惱。」
questions.explain_en: "The eight beginning with restlessness pervade defiled minds: major."

questions.q_zh: 小隨煩惱十種都是假有。
questions.q_en: All ten minor secondary afflictions are designated (not real entities).
questions.explain_zh: 「小十、大三，定是假有。」
questions.explain_en: "The ten minor and three major are definitely designated."

questions.q_zh: 下列哪一個被判為「定是實有」？
questions.q_en: Which is ruled "definitely real"?
questions.explain_zh: 「無慚、無愧、不信、懈怠定是實有。」
questions.explain_en: "Lack of self-respect, lack of decorum, faithlessness and laziness are definitely real."

questions.q_zh: 「隨煩惱」之名的由來是？
